npc:althea-ebonlocke.text: Althea Ebonlocke. Commander Althea Ebonlocke leads the Night Watch, the beleaguered town guard protecting Darkshire from the terrors of Duskwood. A relative of Mayor Ello Ebonlocke, she shoulders the defense of an isolated region abandoned by Stormwind's regular military. She organizes patrols, tasks adventurers with culling local horrors, and coordinates the town's survival against constant monstrous threats. While her relative, Mayor Ello Ebonlocke, handles civil governance within the town hall, Commander Althea directs Darkshire's thin line of physical defense. When Stormwind failed to deploy royal troops to guard Duskwood against creeping horrors, the citizenry formed the Night Watch. Under Althea's steady, unyielding command, these volunteers patrol the fog-shrouded roads, keeping skeletal undead, ferocious wolves, and spiders from overrunning the town perimeter. Althea is pragmatic and understands the limits of her militia. Outnumbered and continually bleeding recruits, she freely enlists passing mercenaries and travelers to thin the threats at Darkshire's doorstep. She directs campaigns against the ghouls and skeletons at the tranquil and sorrowful graveyards of the forest, while remaining vigilant against darker rumors stirring deep in the woods.

npc:asterion.text: Asterion. Asterion is an ancient Highborne spirit bound to the ruins of Bashal'Aran in Darkshore. Once the trusted second to governor Athrikus Narassin ten millennia ago, he was mysteriously imprisoned in a magical moonstone seal that held him through mortal life and into the afterlife. Today, his specter remains shackled to the ruined shrine, surrounded by demonic beasts and dreaming of liberation. Before the Great Sundering shattered ancient Kalimdor, Bashal'Aran and Ameth'Aran were sister cities blessed by Queen Azshara herself. Azshara appointed Athrikus Narassin to govern the twin settlements, and Asterion served as his right hand. Respected for both his physical combat prowess and his command of arcane sorcery, Asterion lived among the people of Bashal'Aran while frequently traveling between the sister cities to manage the needs of their citizens. For reasons lost to time, Asterion fell out of favor with his master. Athrikus fashioned a powerful moonstone seal, forging an inescapable magical cage to confine Asterion within Bashal'Aran. The imprisonment stretched through centuries of agonizing confinement; worse still, when Asterion finally perished, he discovered death offered no release. His spirit remained bound to the ruined shrine, left behind when the world cracked open and demons overran the ancient settlement.

npc:athridas-bearmantle.text: Athridas Bearmantle. Athridas Bearmantle is a night elf druid residing in Dolanaar within the boughs of Teldrassil. Tasked with safeguarding the local settlement, he directs young adventurers to investigate the encroaching corruption affecting the local wildlife and the nearby Gnarlpine furbolgs. Stationed within Dolanaar, Athridas Bearmantle stands as an early line of defense for the night elves emerging from Shadowglen. As the boughs of the newly grown world tree Teldrassil exhibit unnatural signs of decay and unrest, Athridas works tirelessly to coordinate local scouting efforts and protect the peaceful township from surrounding threats. Much of Athridas's concern centers on the neighboring Gnarlpine tribe of furbolgs. Once peaceful neighbors, the Gnarlpine have succumbed to a spreading madness and corruption that poisons their shamans and chieftains, driving them into violent frenzy against the Kaldorei. Athridas mobilizes willing champions to contain the threat and unearth the deeper taint taking root in the wilderness.

npc:blind-mary.text: Blind Mary. Blind Mary is a tormented banshee haunting an abandoned, ruined farmhouse just southeast of Darkshire in Duskwood. Once a vain and beautiful mortal woman, her violent death and transformation drove her to self-inflicted mutilation in grief over what she had become. Before the shadows fell across Duskwood, Mary was known as a striking mortal woman who took immense pride in her beauty, rarely seen without her treasured looking glass. When the undead swept over the region, Mary was slain along with many of her neighbors. Unlike those who found rest in the earth, her spirit lingered on as an ethereal banshee, condemned to wander the mortal realm in a ghastly, translucent form. Awakening to undeath, Mary was overwhelmed by sorrow, horror, and fury at her monstrous reflection. Incapable of enduring the sight of her spectral visage, she clawed out her own eyes with her bare hands so she would never gaze upon herself again. In her agony, she discarded her beloved looking glass, leaving her to drift through her abandoned home as a blind, weeping wraith clutching to faint memories of the mortal life she lost.

npc:captain-grayson.text: Captain Grayson. Captain Grayson is the restless spirit of a pirate captain stationed at the Westfall Lighthouse. Having lost his own life when his ship smashed against the dark coastline, he now watches over the beacon to prevent other sailors from suffering his fate. In life, Grayson captained a vessel along the perilous southern seas of the Eastern Kingdoms. His voyage came to a violent end off the jagged shoals of Westfall on a night when the lighthouse fire had gone dark. Cast upon the rocks, Grayson perished alongside his ship, only to awaken as an earthbound phantom trapped upon the coast. Drawn to the Westfall Lighthouse in death, Grayson hoped to find answers about the afterlife. Instead, he witnessed sheer tragedy. A notorious murloc known as Old Murk-Eye drove the lighthouse keeper and his family away. Though the keepers bravely returned to rekindle the flame, Old Murk-Eye rallied the surrounding murlocs for a second, brutal slaughter. Grayson could only watch helplessly as the family was butchered. With the keepers dead and Westfall crumbling under neglect, Captain Grayson took the solemn burden of the beacon upon his spectral shoulders. He seeks aid from passing adventurers to gather fuel for the great flame and avenge the slaughtered family by hunting down Old Murk-Eye and driving back the coastal murloc tide.

npc:captain-stoutfist.text: Captain Stoutfist. Captain Stoutfist is the dwarven officer in charge of military defenses at Menethil Harbor in the Wetlands. With the Dragonmaw clan pushing aggressively out of their marshland strongholds, Stoutfist coordinates defensive maneuvers and counter-offensives to ensure the vital Alliance port does not fall. Menethil Harbor serves as the principal deepwater port connecting Ironforge and Stormwind to the marshy lowlands of the Wetlands and the sea beyond. As the town's commanding officer, Captain Stoutfist bears the heavy burden of keeping its docks, civilian populace, and garrison secure against surrounding threats. The marshlands are notoriously hazardous, but the biggest peril to the settlement is an organized surge from renegade orcs. The Dragonmaw clan, entrenched within the Wetlands since the Second War, has begun pushing their operations directly toward the roadways and passes. By infiltrating Dun Algaz, they threaten to sever the overland lifeline connecting Loch Modan and Ironforge to Menethil Harbor. Facing a severe shortage of troops, Captain Stoutfist relies on visiting Alliance volunteers recommended by Mountaineer Valstag Ironjaw to stem the tide.

npc:clerk-daltry.text: Clerk Daltry. Clerk Daltry is the civic record keeper stationed in Darkshire Town Hall in Duskwood. Surrounded by ledgers and registry books, he helps investigate the village's past and track down historical records, even if his archives are somewhat neglected and out of date. While Darkshire struggles against encroaching beasts, undead horrors, and supernatural gloom, everyday civic duties fall to Clerk Daltry. Working out of the Darkshire Town Hall alongside Lord Ello Ebonlocke and the local council, Daltry maintains the town's historical ledgers, property rolls, and census data. In a region fractured by disaster, his records are among the few surviving links to the days before Grand Hamlet fell into shadow. Because Darkshire has been cut off from regular Stormwind administration, Daltry's record-keeping is notoriously imperfect. Old documents go missing, ledgers fall behind, and vital town files are frequently misplaced or damaged. Adventurers investigating local cold cases or long-lost residents frequently consult him, only to find that uncovering the truth requires digging through overlooked notes or venturing out into the dangerous woods to recover lost papers.

npc:corithras-moonrage.text: Corithras Moonrage. Corithras Moonrage is a night elf scholar and quest giver stationed in the village of Dolanaar on Teldrassil. He guides newly arrived adventurers in understanding the nature of the great World Tree and tasks them with maintaining its sacred moonwells. Through his lessons, he reveals both the spiritual importance of Teldrassil and the growing burdens carried by the kaldorei. Residing in the shaded settlement of Dolanaar, Corithras Moonrage serves as an instructor to travelers leaving the sheltered bounds of Shadowglen. As young kaldorei venture into the wider boughs of Teldrassil, Corithras ensures they understand the history of their new home. He teaches that survival in this changing era requires vigilance and reverence for the natural order. Much of Corithras's duty revolves around collecting moonwell water for the druids in Darnassus. He directs adventurers to collect pure waters from moonwells across Teldrassil in specially crafted phials for delivery to Fandral Staghelm. Through these trials, he monitors the health of the World Tree and seeks to maintain the delicate balance of the wilderness against creeping corruption.

npc:daphne-stilwell.text: Daphne Stilwell. Daphne Stilwell tends an isolated orchard nestled atop the coastal cliffs of Westfall overlooking the Longshore. Together with her husband Jordan, she fled turmoil in the north and relocated south, quietly aiding the Church of the Holy Light while defending her home from nearby outlaws. Perched on the bluffs to the west of Moonbrook and the exit of the Deadmines, Daphne Stilwell manages a secluded homestead and apple orchard. From below along the Longshore or above on gryphon routes south to Stranglethorn Vale, the small farm looks quiet and unassuming. Yet running a homestead in modern Westfall is anything but safe. Despite the encroaching bandits and roaming scavengers, Daphne diligently works her trees and keeps watch over her isolated patch of land. Before settling in the hills of Westfall, Daphne and her husband Jordan lived in Lordaeron near Pyrewood Village, working in what is now Shadowfang Keep. When darkness and disaster overtook the region, they were driven southward along with thousands of other human refugees. In Stormwind's orbit, Jordan's renowned craftsmanship and Daphne's steady presence led them to forge close ties with the Church of the Holy Light, providing support and holy arms to paladins of the Silver Hand.

npc:delgren-the-purifier.text: Delgren the Purifier. Delgren the Purifier is a human paladin stationed at Maestra's Post on the northern edge of Ashenvale. Operating alongside comrades Balthule Shadowstrike and Feero Ironhand, he aids the night elves in cleansing demonic and shadow magic threatening the frontier, with a particular focus on the sinister Cult of the Dark Strand. Human paladins are a rare sight deep within the ancient forests of Kalimdor, but Delgren the Purifier arrived with a mission. Affiliated with the Argent Dawn, Delgren traveled west with a cadre of holy warriors determined to assist the Alliance's new night elf allies against the lingering evils of demons and undead remnants from the Third War. Stationed near the border of Darkshore and Ashenvale, he maintains a watchful vigil over travelers passing south from Auberdine. Despite his fierce devotion to the Holy Light and zealous nickname, Delgren possesses an unusual perspective on Kalimdor's tangled politics. Much to the annoyance and disdain of his conservative superiors, he took the time to learn Orcish. This rare linguistic skill hints at an unconventional mind—one that seeks to understand the enemies and neighbors sharing this untamed continent rather than relying solely on blind dogma.

npc:denalan.text: Denalan. Denalan is an accomplished night elf herbalist and botanist who tends a quiet lakeside plot along the eastern shore of Lake Al'Ameth. Working under a simple awning, he devotes his days to studying the island's plant life and seeking botanical remedies for the strange corruption affecting Teldrassil. He frequently enlists young adventurers to gather samples, study violent timberlings, and test enchanted soils. While many kaldorei focus on martial vigilance or high druidic rites, Denalan pursues the patient, meticulous craft of herbalism. Stationed along the tranquil eastern banks of Lake Al'Ameth, he has established a modest research camp consisting of a cloth awning, simple field tools, and tidy rows of cultivated planter boxes. Rather than retreating to the grand barrows of Darnassus, he prefers to remain close to the loam, directly examining the unusual flora that has sprouted since the planting of the new World Tree. Denalan's research is far more than an academic curiosity; it addresses the growing unrest among Teldrassil's native wildlife. The timberlings, normally docile woodland beings of wood and sprout, have turned increasingly aggressive. Denalan enchants specialized soil to nurse wild seeds in captivity and analyze how malignant forces seep into the root systems. By studying strange specimens like shimmering fronds, glowing fruit, and moss-twined growths, he seeks to isolate whatever dark taint is troubling the forest boughs.

npc:dirania-silvershine.text: Dirania Silvershine. Dirania Silvershine is a night elf resident of Shadowglen in Teldrassil. Deeply loyal and observant, she watches over the tranquil grove and looks out for her companion Iverron when his reckless ventures land him in peril. Dirania stands among the tranquil boughs of Shadowglen, the secluded vale where young night elves begin their service to Kalimdor and the Alliance. While many in the barrow mounds and sanctuaries look to broad spiritual duties, Dirania stays mindful of those nearest to her, attentive to the quiet dangers that stir even in the heart of Teldrassil. Dirania's immediate concern is her companion Iverron. Overeager and careless around the poisonous woodland creatures creeping across the glen, Iverron frequently gets into trouble. When he succumbs to a venomous bite from the local webwood spiders, Dirania takes it upon herself to seek out willing hands to gather ingredients and prepare a remedy before the venom takes a permanent toll.

npc:dorn-plainstalker.text: Dorn Plainstalker. Dorn Plainstalker is a solitary tauren elder residing in the Weathered Nook overlooking the canyons of Thousand Needles. He serves as an overseer of traditional rite of passage trials, challenging Horde adventurers to prove their character and fortitude. Through trials of faith, endurance, strength, and lore, he tests whether travelers are worthy servants of the Earth Mother and their people. Secluded in a shallow cave high atop the canyon ridges of the Weathered Nook, Dorn Plainstalker lives apart from the bustle of Freewind Post. Reaching his mountain redoubt requires winding along the sheer northern cliffs overlooking the towering mesas below. From this quiet vantage point, Dorn maintains ancient customs and judges those who seek guidance in the harsh southern barrens. Dorn Plainstalker guides pilgrims through a demanding series of tests meant to measure the core virtues of a tauren champion: faith, endurance, strength, and lore. Rather than mere exercises in brute force, these trials force aspirants to confront fear, leap blindly into the unknown, outlast cunning wilderness predators, and ponder the sacred history of Kalimdor before claiming their final passage.

npc:elling-trias.text: Elling Trias. Elling Trias manages Trias' Cheese, a small storefront nestled in the bustling Trade District of Stormwind City. While he presents himself as a jovial and passionate purveyor of dairy, he quietly operates as one of the kingdom's most connected information brokers. Behind wheels of cheese and cordial banter, Trias maintains an ear to the ground that reaches across continents. To the casual customer strolling the Trade District, Elling Trias is merely an artisan dedicated to fine curds, working his shop alongside his wife Elaine and son Ben. He enthusiastically hawks wheels of cheese and chats amicably with townsfolk. Yet those in the know understand that Trias' Cheese is one of the most reliable fronts in Stormwind. The steady hum of city commerce provides perfect cover for operatives, courtiers, and adventurers who need to trade quiet words without drawing the attention of the city watch. Elling's network of informants and allies is staggering for a shopkeeper. He maintains ties with Master Mathias Shaw of SI:7, coordinates with Church contacts like Bishop DeLavey, and corresponds with agents as far afield as Darkshire, Theramore Isle, and the distant Plaguelands near Hearthglen. When odd rumors surface—whether concerning highway bandits or quiet movements in the countryside—Trias often pieces the puzzle together long before the royal court takes notice.

npc:first-mate-fitzsimmons.text: First Mate Fitzsimmons. First Mate Fitzsimmons is a ragged, reeking sailor who spends his days drinking outside the Deepwater Tavern in Menethil Harbor. Once the first mate aboard the Wave Mistress of the Kul Tiras Third Fleet, he is the sole known living survivor of the fleet's destruction during the Second War. Haunted by the tragedy, he seeks willing adventurers to face the restless spirits of his drowned comrades. Lounging outside the Deepwater Tavern amid the damp salt air of Menethil Harbor, First Mate Fitzsimmons is an easy man to overlook—or avoid entirely, given his unwashed stench. To most patrons, he is just another broken old salt drinking his memories away. Yet those willing to sit and listen will hear harrowing tales of a proud fleet brought low by fire and claw. During the Second War, Fitzsimmons served as first mate aboard the Wave Mistress, part of the Kul Tiras Third Fleet dispatched to fight the Horde. Off the coast of the Wetlands, the fleet was ambushed and incinerated by enslaved red dragons flown by Dragonmaw orcs. The ships were shattered and sunk, leaving Fitzsimmons as the only man to drag himself ashore alive.

npc:furen-longbeard.text: Furen Longbeard. Furen Longbeard is a master dwarven armorer stationed within Stormwind City's bustling Dwarven District. Apprenticed under the renowned smith Grimand Elmore, he specializes in crafting heavy protective gear and sturdy mail for seasoned defenders of the Alliance. Warriors across the kingdom seek out his metallurgical expertise to forge specialized, battle-ready armor. Furen Longbeard plies his craft far from the great forges of Ironforge, making his home instead among the cobblestones and soot of Stormwind's Dwarven District. Like many of his kin, Furen brought traditional dwarven metallurgy south to support the rebuilding and defense of the kingdom. Working amidst blazing hearths and clanging anvils, he maintains strong ties with other artisans throughout the city and beyond. Taught by the venerable craftsman Grimand Elmore, Furen has perfected techniques for treating heavy mail and plate to withstand extreme battlefield punishment. Promising young warriors seeking durable protection often turn to Furen, who requires rare ores, specialized components, and exotic reagents from distant corners of the world to fashion his signature fire-hardened armor.

npc:gakin-the-darkbinder.text: Gakin the Darkbinder. Gakin the Darkbinder is a master warlock operating covertly deep beneath The Slaughtered Lamb tavern in Stormwind's Mage Quarter. He instructs aspiring Alliance practitioners in the dark arts, testing their resolve before initiating rituals to summon and bind otherworldly demons to their service. While Stormwind's mages practice openly in their towering sanctuaries, practitioners of shadow and fel must dwell where prying eyes cannot reach. Hidden below the taproom of The Slaughtered Lamb is a damp crypt-like cellar equipped with summoning circles and grim tomes. Gakin serves as the anchor of this hidden conclave, ensuring that young warlocks learn discipline and restraint before unleashing horrors they cannot control. Gakin's expertise lies in demonology and binding rituals. Initiates who earn his notice are sent across the kingdom to acquire rare relics and ingredients—from stolen bloodstone talismans to corrupt wood from the dark forests. Once the reagents are assembled, Gakin oversees rituals in the crypt's summoning circle, forcing novitiates to subjugate voidwalkers and succubi in life-or-death trials of willpower.

npc:gaxim-rustfizzle.text: Gaxim Rustfizzle. Gaxim Rustfizzle is an ambitious gnome scholar and tinker stationed at a small Alliance camp along the Webwinder Path in Stonetalon Mountains. A representative of the Enlightened Assembly of Arcanology, Alchemy and Engineering Sciences, he seeks to prove to skeptical night elves that advanced artifice and alchemy can preserve their woodland realm. His scientific curiosity is matched by a fierce vendetta against the destructive operations of the Venture Company. While night elves traditionally rely on ancient druidism and nature magic, Gaxim Rustfizzle arrived in the craggy passes of Stonetalon to demonstrate a radically different perspective. Representing the Enlightened Assembly of Arcanology, Alchemy and Engineering Sciences, he genuinely believes that calculated mechanisms and chemical solutions can defend and restore Kalimdor's wilderness just as effectively as prayers to Elune. Camped alongside the sentinel Kaela Shadowspear on the Webwinder Path, he works tirelessly to convince his tall, reclusive allies of engineering's ecological merits. Much of Gaxim's energy is channeled against the Venture Company, whose clear-cutting and industrial greed desecrate nearby Windshear Crag. Believing that crude goblin machinery deserves neither respect nor mercy, Gaxim coordinates covert operations and volatile chemical sabotage against their logging operations. To him, crippling their shredders and stealing their schematics is not merely tactical warfare—it is a practical demonstration that superior gnomish intellect always triumphs over careless corporate plunder.

npc:gwennyth-bly-leggonde.text: Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde. Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde is a night elf residing in the coastal port of Auberdine. Stationed along the misty Darkshore coast, she watches the tides and directs travelers to investigate the strange remains washing ashore. Her concerns center on the mysterious sea creatures and massive turtles whose carcasses have begun littering the northern beaches. Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde makes her home in Auberdine, the bustling seaside haven of Darkshore. While many in town concern themselves with the forest or shipping across the Veiled Sea, Gwennyth keeps her gaze firmly on the coastline. The tides have recently turned grim, depositing the remains of colossal marine life onto the surf. To understand what is happening in the waters offshore, she relies on willing adventurers to scour the sands, retrieve skeletal samples, and bring back answers. The beaches north and south of Auberdine have seen an alarming influx of beached sea creatures and ancient sea turtles. Rather than letting their deaths go unnoticed, Gwennyth tasks travelers with inspecting these fallen titans. By studying the bones and discovering what drove these beasts ashore or took their lives, she hopes to piece together the hidden perils lurking off the shores of northern Kalimdor.

npc:high-executor-darthalia.text: High Executor Darthalia. High Executor Darthalia is a high-ranking Forsaken military commander stationed at Tarren Mill in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Acting under the direct authority of Lady Sylvanas Windrunner and Varimathras, she directs Forsaken operations against the human stronghold of Southshore and local Syndicate brigands. Her leadership is central to securing the Horde's southern flank in Lordaeron. Operating out of Tarren Mill, High Executor Darthalia serves as the operational commander for Forsaken forces throughout the Hillsbrad Foothills. Her primary strategic concern is halting the expansion of human resistance, keeping the Alliance forces in Southshore contained, and hunting down the lawless Syndicate rogues infesting the surrounding countryside. Every offensive push into southern Hillsbrad flows directly through her command. Under direct orders originating from the Undercity's high leadership—the Banshee Queen and her dreadlord lieutenant, Varimathras—Darthalia oversees the relentless attrition war across Hillsbrad. She coordinates scouting missions, targeted strikes against human leadership, and bounties on dangerous outlaws who threaten the Forsaken hold on northern Lordaeron.

npc:illiyana.text: Illiyana. Illiyana is an ancient dryad stationed in southwestern Ashenvale, dedicated to protecting the woodland from ancient corruption. Wandering near the Shrine of Aessina, she rallies champions of the Alliance to push back against the vicious satyrs that plague the ancient groves. Her vigilance represents the enduring bond between the daughters of Cenarius and the night elven wilderness. Like all dryads, Illiyana is one of the daughters of the demigod Cenarius. Peaceful yet fiercely protective of wild lands, she patrols the woods of southwestern Ashenvale. As dark forces stir and the woodlands suffer under creeping corruption, Illiyana keeps watch over sacred relics and groves, acting as a steward for nature's primal sanctity. Illiyana's primary concern in the region is the lingering blight of the satyrs. These twisted, demonic creatures continuously seek to corrupt the glades and endanger her dryad sisters. Illiyana frequently enlists passing travelers to strike down these vile abominations and recover lost artifacts, including the Branch of Cenarius, to ensure the woods remain sheltered from demonic taint.

npc:jaina-proudmoore.text: Jaina Proudmoore. Lady Jaina Proudmoore is the ruler of Theramore Isle and the most powerful human sorceress alive. Formerly a star pupil of Dalaran's Kirin Tor, she led the survivors of Lordaeron across the Great Sea and now strives to maintain a fragile peace between the Alliance and the New Horde. The daughter of Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore of Kul Tiras, Jaina showed remarkable aptitude for the arcane at an early age and studied under Archmage Antonidas in Dalaran. During the Third War, she investigated the mysterious Plague of Undeath alongside Prince Arthas Menethil, witnessing firsthand the tragic downfall of Lordaeron. Guided by the warnings of the Prophet Medivh, she rallied an expedition of human survivors and set sail westward to the forgotten continent of Kalimdor. There, her forces forged an unprecedented alliance with Thrall's Horde and the night elves, standing together atop Mount Hyjal to defeat Archimonde and shatter the Burning Legion's invasion. Following the Legion's defeat, Jaina founded the island citadel of Theramore off the coast of Dustwallow Marsh, establishing the primary bastion of the Alliance in southern Kalimdor. Her commitment to diplomacy was tested to its limits when her father arrived seeking vengeance against the orcs; Jaina refused to support his war, stepping aside as Thrall's forces slew the Grand Admiral to prevent Kalimdor from plunging into another devastating conflict. Today, she rules Theramore as a steadfast advocate for coexistence, working closely with Warchief Thrall while anchoring the Alliance's presence against rising local tensions.

npc:jern-hornhelm.text: Jern Hornhelm. Jern Hornhelm is a dwarven miner affiliated with the Explorers' League, stationed in the town of Thelsamar. He coordinates vital logistics and communication between the settlement, Ironforge, and the archaeological dig site deeper in Loch Modan. Adventurers frequently assist him with shuttling mining supplies and progress reports across the region. Stationed within the rustic town of Thelsamar, Jern Hornhelm plays a key logistical role for dwarven operations throughout Loch Modan. While dwarven scholars and field teams venture out into the wilderness to unearth their ancestral past, maintaining consistent supply chains remains essential. Jern ensures that vital resources, tools, and communications reach the active dig sites safely. As a member of the Explorers' League, Jern bridges the gap between field archaeologists and the League's leadership in the Hall of Explorers in Ironforge. Sites such as Ironband's Excavation rely heavily on blasting powder, equipment, and regular dispatches to keep work moving forward. Jern enlists reliable travelers to navigate the trogg-infested roads and keep the dig fully operational.

npc:jitters.text: Jitters. Jitters is a terrified, half-starved human hiding among the ruins of Raven Hill in Duskwood. He clings to scraps of food and struggles to speak about the horrors he has witnessed. Found shivering amid the dilapidated houses of Raven Hill, Jitters lives in constant terror of the predators stalking Duskwood's western trails. He relies on passing adventurers for simple sustenance, desperate for food while keeping a frantic eye on the encroaching shadows. His skittish mannerisms and uncanny reflex for leaping clear of sudden danger earned him his moniker long ago, but his frantic paranoia is born from firsthand encounters with horrific horrors.

npc:jordan-stilwell.text: Jordan Stilwell. Jordan Stilwell is a skilled human weaponsmith stationed outside the snowy Gates of Ironforge in Dun Morogh. Though originally meant to become a paladin of the Holy Light, he followed his father's craft to become an artisan whose work serves paladins across the Alliance. He is best known for forging Verigan's Fist in honor of his old friend, Bosch Verigan. Though Jordan Stilwell was expected to take holy vows and become a paladin within the Church of the Holy Light, he ultimately chose the way of the forge. He followed in his father's footsteps, taking up his father's enchanted smithing hammer. Jordan refined his craft under the tutelage of the dwarven blacksmith Bailor Stonehand. Despite setting aside the mantle of an anointed holy warrior, Jordan remains deeply faithful to the Light, dedicating his extraordinary craftsmanship to outfitting champions who fight in its name. Long before setting up shop in the biting cold of Dun Morogh, Jordan served as a smith at the keep of Baron Silverlaine in Silverpine Forest. When Archmage Arugal unleashed the feral worgen upon the fortress, turning it into the cursed bastion known as Shadowfang Keep, Jordan managed to escape the bloodshed. Forced to abandon his forge and his former home, he eventually found refuge among the dwarves of Dun Morogh.

npc:laurna-morninglight.text: Laurna Morninglight. Laurna Morninglight is a night elf priest trainer residing in the tranquil settlement of Dolanaar within Teldrassil. Devoted to the Sisterhood of Elune, she guides budding acolytes emerging from Shadowglen in the spiritual rites and healing graces of the Moon Goddess. Her teachings prepare young night elf priests for the growing threats encroaching on the boughs of the World Tree. Situated amidst the boughs of Dolanaar, Laurna Morninglight serves as one of the primary mentors for young priests who have completed their initial rites in Shadowglen. As new initiates step out into the broader reaches of Teldrassil, she instructs them on expanding their communion with Elune, balancing the light of healing with defensive rites necessary to survive an increasingly hostile wild. Priestcraft among the kaldorei is deeply intertwined with the worship of Elune rather than the abstract Holy Light revered by humans and dwarves. Laurna tasks her students with spiritual labors such as receiving sacred robes and healing a wounded Sentinel. Through these traditions, acolytes learn that their powers are direct gifts of the Mother Moon, meant to preserve and mend the kaldorei people.

npc:lieutenant-farren-orinelle.text: Lieutenant Farren Orinelle. Lieutenant Farren Orinelle is an officer of the Stormwind army currently stationed at the Southshore inn in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Deeply unhappy with his frontier posting, he spends most of his time drinking while outsourcing his duties to passing travelers. His primary military assignment is dealing with the encroaching murlocs along the coast, a chore he eagerly delegates in hopes of securing a transfer back south. Lieutenant Farren Orinelle did not choose Southshore. Dispatched far from Stormwind City, the lieutenant finds the damp, contested shores of Hillsbrad a miserable step down from the civilized comforts of the capital. Instead of patrolling the fields or coordinating defenses with his commanding officer, Marshal Redpath, Orinelle has practically taken up permanent residence inside Southshore's inn. His days are spent sulking, drinking, and dreaming of an official transfer order that will return him to the south. Despite his comfortable seat at the tavern, Orinelle still answers to Marshal Redpath, who tasked the lieutenant with clearing out the murlocs swarming the nearby shoreline. Unwilling to soil his boots in coastal mud, Orinelle relies on wandering adventurers to cull the creatures and gather proof of their demise. He hopes that presenting tangible results back to his superiors will show his duty is accomplished, hastening his eventual recall to Stormwind.

npc:lord-ello-ebonlocke.text: Lord Ello Ebonlocke. Lord Ello Ebonlocke is the mayor of Darkshire and the leader of its governing council, stationed inside the Darkshire Town Hall. Surrounded by darkness and creeping horrors, he struggles daily to maintain order and protect his besieged citizens despite receiving little aid from Stormwind. Seated in the gloom of the Darkshire Town Hall, Lord Ello Ebonlocke bears the heavy burden of governing a settlement on the brink of ruin. Once part of the prosperous rural haven known as Grand Hamlet, Darkshire is now smothered by perpetual shadow and besieged by ravenous ghouls, skeletal abominations, and feral beasts. Ello presides over the Council of Darkshire, striving against impossible odds to keep the remnants of civilization functioning while Stormwind turns a blind eye to their plight. Because Stormwind's garrison refuses to spare soldiers for the borderlands, Darkshire relies almost entirely on local volunteer militias like the Night Watch, commanded by his relative, Althea Ebonlocke. When neighboring leaders like Magistrate Solomon of Lakeshire plead for reinforcements to combat Blackrock orcs, Lord Ebonlocke must make agonizing choices. As he solemnly explains to messengers from Redridge, Darkshire cannot spare a single blade: sending their guards beyond the forest's edge would leave their own homes to be instantly overrun by the surrounding evils.

npc:maggran-earthbinder.text: Maggran Earthbinder. Maggran Earthbinder is a grizzled tauren veteran appointed by High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof to lead the Horde encampment at Sun Rock Retreat. Hardened by a lifetime of brutal conflict, he oversees the defense of the craggy valleys of Stonetalon against ravenous beasts and aggressive harpy covens. Though wearied by countless battles, he remains a steadfast guardian of the settlement. Maggran Earthbinder was sent into the Stonetalon Mountains by High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof himself. A veteran of countless skirmishes and bloody campaigns, Maggran admits that age and violence have hardened his heart, stripping away the natural gentleness typical of his people. Sun Rock Retreat was meant to be both an outpost under his steady command and a place of respite, where warm winds and mountain sunshine might soothe his battle-worn spirit. Even in Stonetalon, Maggran finds little peace. As overseer of Sun Rock Retreat, he coordinates defense efforts against the Bloodfury harpies nesting in the peaks and marshals fighters to counter predatory perils across the crags. Having once survived an ambush by the giant spider Besseleth herself, Maggran holds no illusions about the deadly wilderness around them and frequently enlists travelers to eliminate deadly regional predators before they overrun the outpost.

npc:malfurion-stormrage.text: Malfurion Stormrage. Malfurion Stormrage is the first mortal druid and the revered leader of the night elves alongside High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind. Renowned for defeating the Burning Legion in both the War of the Ancients and the Third War, he is venerated as the Shan'do, or honored teacher. Currently, he lies trapped in a comatose slumber within the Emerald Dream, leaving the kaldorei without his waking guidance. Ten thousand years ago, before the Great Sundering shattered ancient Kalimdor, Malfurion studied under the demigod Cenarius. While Queen Azshara and her Highborne caste delved dangerously into the arcane energies of the Well of Eternity, Malfurion turned toward the primal forces of nature, becoming Azeroth's first mortal druid. His suspicions regarding the Highborne proved tragically correct when Azshara's reckless sorcery pierced the veil and summoned Sargeras and the Burning Legion into Azeroth, igniting the catastrophic War of the Ancients. Alongside Cenarius, Tyrande Whisperwind, and his twin brother Illidan, Malfurion spearheaded the resistance that halted the demon onslaught and closed the portal over the Well of Eternity. Following the world's shattering, Malfurion committed the druids to the Emerald Dream to rebuild and protect Azeroth's living tapestry. Ten millennia later, Tyrande awakened him from his long barrow sleep to confront Archimonde during the Third War, where he rallied the forest spirits at Mount Hyjal to shatter the Burning Legion once more. Following the Third War, Malfurion returned to his slumber within the Moonglade to commune with the Emerald Dream and replenish his spent power. However, his spirit has failed to return to his physical body, plunging him into an unnatural, comatose state. In Darnassus, Archdruid Fandral Staghelm has assumed the temporal duties of leadership among the Cenarion Circle, while Tyrande and the sisterhood watch anxiously for signs of their great Shan'do's waking.

npc:marshal-dughan.text: Marshal Dughan. Marshal Dughan is the commanding officer of the Stormwind Army detachment stationed in Goldshire. Tasked with protecting the heart of Elwynn Forest, he finds his local garrison stretched thin against growing incursions of kobolds, gnolls, and bandits. To keep the crossroads town and surrounding farmsteads safe, he relies heavily on independent adventurers. Stationed prominently in Goldshire outside the Lion's Pride Inn, Marshal Dughan bears the heavy burden of keeping Elwynn Forest secure while Stormwind's military resources are tied up elsewhere. The surrounding woods are steadily deteriorating: vermin choke the mines, gnolls mass along the riverbanks, and highwaymen harass travelers along the King's Road. With too few footmen under his direct command, Dughan orchestrates local defense by directing fresh recruits to reinforce outposts and scout contested ground. Dughan's immediate concerns lie with the kobold infestations overrunning Fargodeep and Jasperlode Mines, threatening Goldshire's vital mineral output. To the west, Riverpaw gnolls led by the notorious Hogger press hard against Westbrook Garrison. To the east, Dughan is forced to confront reports from Guard Thomas concerning vicious murlocs slaughtering patrols along the river. Managing these overlapping crises with limited manpower keeps the marshal in constant need of capable mercenaries.

npc:marshal-marris.text: Marshal Marris. Marshal Marris is the beleaguered military officer commanding the town watch at Lakeshire. Stationed near the town's bridge, he coordinates defense operations against the massive Blackrock orc invasion pressing down from the heights of the Redridge Mountains. With Stormwind's army absent, he relies on visiting adventurers to blunt the horde's advances. Lakeshire stands on the brink of collapse, caught between the gnolls to the west and the terrifying military might of the Blackrock clan to the east. Marshal Marris oversees the guard line at the town's primary bridge, but his resources are depleted and his soldiers are spread impossibly thin. With the kingdom of Stormwind withholding royal reinforcements, Marris carries the heavy burden of keeping the township from being overwhelmed by brute force. Recognizing that defense alone will not save Redridge, Marris orchestrates decisive offensive strikes against the orc encampments. He directs mercenaries to cull the Blackrock warriors, dismantle their shadowcasters, and ultimately hunt down Tharil'zun, the menacing commander entrenched inside the ruins of Stonewatch Keep. His orders aim to break the command structure of the orcs before an all-out assault crushes Lakeshire completely.

npc:marshal-mcbride.text: Marshal McBride. Marshal Douglas McBride is the commander of the Stormwind garrison stationed at Northshire Abbey. Tasked with the defense of Northshire Valley, he directs freshly arrived recruits against the rising kobold infestation threatening local farms and mines. He serves as the primary military authority for newcomers beginning their service to the kingdom of Stormwind. Stationed right outside Northshire Abbey, Marshal Douglas McBride represents the direct authority of the Stormwind Army in this quiet valley. While the abbey itself is an enclave of faith and learning, rising turmoil across the kingdom has stretched military garrisons thin. McBride must maintain peace and secure the valley's food and resource supplies with only a handful of sworn guards and an influx of green recruits seeking training under the abbey's masters. McBride's primary headache is the sudden aggression of local vermin. Kobolds, once merely a nuisance, have overrun the surrounding woods and seized Echo Ridge Mine—a vital local asset. Lacking the regular soldiers needed to clear them out, McBride marshals paladins, warriors, and other novices to push back the tunneling pests and uncover the extent of the infestation before the valley is completely choked off.

npc:mathias-shaw.text: Mathias Shaw. Master Mathias Shaw is the leader of SI:7, the covert intelligence agency of the Kingdom of Stormwind. Operating from the shadows of Old Town, he directs spies and scouts to protect the realm from internal conspiracies and external horrors alike. Mathias Shaw stands as Stormwind's foremost spymaster and assassin. From SI:7's discreet headquarters tucked behind the barracks in Old Town, Shaw coordinates a covert network that spans the Eastern Kingdoms and beyond. Pragmatic, calculating, and fiercely loyal to the House of Wrynn, he operates on the philosophy that Stormwind's safety depends just as much on unseen daggers and stolen missives as it does on gleaming armor and palace garrisons. While domestic insurrection consumes Westfall and Elwynn, Shaw's attention is constantly drawn outward to lethal unknowns. When reports reached him of bizarre Forsaken operations in the Eastern Plaguelands, he dispatched five of his finest agents to investigate. Only one returned alive—babbling in terror about "Nathanos" and a "Blightcaller" before dying in his sleep. Shaw relies on trusted independent champions to venture where his scouts vanish, seeking to pierce the gloom gathering at the kingdom's borders.

npc:motega-firemane.text: Motega Firemane. Motega Firemane is a tauren scholar stationed at Whitereach Post in Thousand Needles. Dedicated to cataloging the dangerous wildlife of the canyon, he finds his studies disrupted by a vengeful wind serpent spirit and the reckless misadventures of his young assistant. Four years following the Third War, Motega Firemane journeyed south into Thousand Needles to observe and record the distinct beasts surviving among the towering mesas. Accompanied by his youthful assistant, Pao'ka Swiftmountain—whose protective father was reluctant to let him leave Mulgore—Motega set up camp alongside Kanati Greycloud at Whitereach Post. While his original calling was quiet natural observation, the harsh perils of the canyon floor continually demand a more martial approach to survival.

npc:orgrim-doomhammer.text: Orgrim Doomhammer. Orgrim Doomhammer was the supreme Warchief of the Old Horde throughout the Second War, remembered as one of the greatest orc warriors in history. Though he died liberating the internment camps in the Arathi Highlands, his legacy endures in the capital of Orgrimmar and through Thrall, who inherited his mighty warhammer and black plate armor. Originally second-in-command to Blackhand of the Blackrock clan, Orgrim refused the demonic blood offered by Gul'dan, though he concealed his doubts beneath fierce loyalty. Near the close of the First War, disgusted by the Shadow Council's treachery and the murder of his childhood friend Durotan, Orgrim slew Blackhand in honorable combat. Assuming the mantle of Warchief, he ruthlessly purged Gul'dan's warlocks and led the Horde across the Eastern Kingdoms during the Second War. Though a devastating strategist who pushed human kingdoms to the brink of ruin, he was ultimately defeated and captured outside Blackrock Spire after the betrayal of Gul'dan split his forces. Escaping human captivity, Doomhammer lived in hiding until he met Thrall, Durotan's orphaned son. Reinvigorated by the young shaman's vision, Orgrim rallied what was left of the orcish clans to storm the internment camps and break their people free. During a fierce battle at an encampment in the Arathi Highlands, the Warchief was struck down from behind by a lance. As he lay dying, he bestowed his black plate armor, his ancestral weapon—the Doomhammer—and the title of Warchief upon Thrall. In his honor, the liberated outpost was renamed Hammerfall, and the newly founded capital in Durotar was christened Orgrimmar.

npc:priestess-alathea.text: Priestess Alathea. Priestess Alathea is a night elf priest trainer residing within the tranquil halls of the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus. Devoted to the Moon Goddess, she guides novitiates in the sacred arts and racial blessings bestowed by Elune. Her teachings help night elf practitioners attune their minds to defensive prayers and celestial magic. Standing within the soaring silver heights of Darnassus's grandest sanctuary, Priestess Alathea serves the Sisterhood of Elune as an instructor and spiritual guide. As night elf initiates progress beyond the quiet boughs of Shadowglen, they are directed to the Temple of the Moon to deepen their covenant with the Goddess. Alathea stands among the priestesses ready to impart sacred knowledge to those who dedicate their lives to healing, warding, and divine light. Unlike priests of the Holy Light who draw strength strictly from human and dwarven traditions, kaldorei priests draw directly upon the grace of Elune. Alathea plays a key role in testing and granting blessings tailored to night elves, such as Stars of Elune and Elune's Grace. Through her guidance, acolytes learn how to weave starlight into shields of swiftness and defensive power to survive the growing perils facing Kalimdor.

npc:rejold-barleybrew.text: Rejold Barleybrew. Rejold Barleybrew is a master dwarven brewer stationed in the lakeside settlement of Brewnall Village in western Dun Morogh. Devoted to perfecting hearty mountain spirits, he regularly enlists travelers to gather regional ingredients and test his potent recipes across the snowy valley. In Dun Morogh, brewing is treated not merely as trade, but as a defining art form. Rejold Barleybrew embodies this tradition from Brewnall Village, an outpost nestled near the frozen lake of the Iceflow River. Rather than settling for common tavern swill, Rejold continually refines his blends, seeking rare hops, mountain minerals, and pristine ice water to produce stouts capable of warming the stoutest dwarven warriors. Rejold is relentless in his quest for ideal flavor profiles, sending adventurous spirits across Dun Morogh to collect vital components for drinks like Shimmer Stout. Whether trading favors with the siege pilots of Steelgrill's Depot or arranging deliveries to thirsty patrons, his work ensures that the cold, trogg-plagued roads of Dun Morogh remain tolerable with an ample supply of hearty ale.

npc:rethiel-the-greenwarden.text: Rethiel the Greenwarden. Rethiel the Greenwarden is an ancient, sentient bog beast residing in the Green Belt within the Wetlands. Deeply attuned to the natural balance of the marsh, he watches over the land and enlists travelers to cull threats that disrupt its harmony. Standing amidst the damp thickets of the Green Belt, Rethiel is a towering creature of moss, peat, and primal plant life. While many bog beasts in the marshlands wander aimlessly as aggressive predators, Rethiel possesses a rare, conscious awareness and a sorrowful voice. He perceives the wetlands not merely as murky terrain, but as a living ecosystem that currently cries out under the weight of foreign predation and corruption. Rethiel seeks to alleviate the suffering of the Wetlands by dispatching sympathetic adventurers against its major agitators. He urges visitors to hunt down destructive Mosshide gnolls who ravage the wildlife, strip them of the crude flints they use to burn the marsh's living trees, and thin out the diseased fen creepers that fester in the marsh waters. Through these cullings, he hopes to restore peace to the wounded soil.

npc:rorian-the-dayseeker.text: Rorian the Dayseeker. Rorian the Dayseeker is an elder Skyborne figure situated in Thendal Village on Zephras Isle. He oversees the initiation of young fledglings as they discover their calling, step into maturity, and attune themselves to the natural elements of their homeland. Under his watchful guidance, newcomers learn the fundamentals of survival, tradition, and service to their community. Within the serene confines of Thendal Village on Zephras Isle, Rorian the Dayseeker stands as one of the primary mentors for the fledgling Skyborne. Revered for his experience and calm wisdom, Rorian directs youth during their crucial transition into adulthood. It is under his instruction that initiates undertake their traditional rite of passage, marking their readiness to defend and support their island home. Beyond fundamental trials, Rorian points promising initiates toward specialized paths suited to their talents. Whether an aspiring warrior, hunter, rogue, mage, shaman, or druid, fledglings are directed by Rorian to dedicated trainers across the isle. He also alerts them to elemental disturbances disrupting the island's harmony, instilling an enduring duty to preserve balance across the windswept heights.

npc:senani-thunderheart.text: Senani Thunderheart. Senani Thunderheart is a tauren huntress stationed at Splintertree Post in Ashenvale, just north of the Barrens. Serving the Horde, she tests the mettle of passing travelers by challenging them to pursue the fierce wild predators that roam the ancient forest. Through her trials, hunters prove their skill while thinning the deadly beasts prowling near Horde territory. Found keeping camp at Splintertree Post, Senani Thunderheart represents the hunting traditions of the tauren amid the shadowed groves of Ashenvale. Far from the open plains of Mulgore, she directs Horde adventurers to test their tracking and combat prowess against the forest's apex beasts. She views the hunt as both an honorable challenge and a necessary ritual to survive in an untamed, contested land. Senani oversees the traditional hunting trials of Ashenvale, directing hunters toward three notorious predators: the bear Ursangous, the cat Shadumbra, and the hippogryph Sharptalon. Claiming their tokens—a paw, a head, and a claw—is a rite of passage that demonstrates a hunter's respect for the land and dominion over its fiercest denizens.

npc:senir-whitebeard.text: Senir Whitebeard. Senir Whitebeard is a dwarven dignitary and field agent stationed outside the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos. Serving as a special envoy from the Senate of Ironforge, he is tasked with monitoring the growing threats encircling Dun Morogh. His mission centers on evaluating the Frostmane troll offensive and reporting their movements directly back to the dwarven leadership. While most travelers visit Kharanos for its bustling inn and famous stout, Senir Whitebeard is here on official business. As a representative sent directly by the Senate of Ironforge, his presence highlights how seriously the high halls take the destabilization of Dun Morogh. He serves as an essential bridge between local scouts facing danger on the snowy frontier and the legislators arguing policy behind the city's stone gates. Senir's primary concern is the escalating aggression of the Frostmane trolls. Displaced and desperate in the frozen crags, the trolls have begun pushing dangerously close to dwarven settlements and roads. Rather than charging into battle himself, the venerable envoy gathers reconnaissance on troll positions, particularly around their stronghold, compiling meticulous reports so Ironforge's military commanders can strike decisively.

npc:shael-dryn.text: Shael'dryn. Shael'dryn is an inquisitive dryad residing beside the Moonwell of Purity, east of Iris Lake in Ashenvale. She serves as a vital contact for night elf scouts investigating forest corruption. She plays a pivotal role in aiding Astranaar's sentinels with cleansing relics to combat demonic and foul influences spreading across the wilderness. Stationed beside the Moonwell of Purity, Shael'dryn keeps watch alongside the night elf sentinels guarding the eastern approaches of the forest. When corruption surfaces among the local wildlife or tainted relics threaten the land's harmony, her deep natural understanding allows her to guide adventurers through the steps required to restore spiritual balance.

npc:sprite-jumpsprocket.text: Sprite Jumpsprocket. Sprite Jumpsprocket is an apprentice gnome engineer currently residing in the busy Dwarven District of Stormwind City. Like many gnomes who sought refuge following the fall of Gnomeregan, she pursues technical craft and innovation alongside her fellow tinkers. Her presence highlights the thriving community of dwarven and gnomish artisans who keep the capital city supplied with gears, gadgets, and mechanical expertise. In the soot-covered streets and bustling workshops of the Dwarven District, gnomes and dwarves work shoulder-to-shoulder forging metal and designing intricate contraptions. Sprite Jumpsprocket serves as an apprentice engineer in this vibrant hub. Having integrated into the kingdom's capital, apprentice tinkers like Sprite hone their craft under experienced masters, contributing their inventive minds to the everyday mechanisms and technological marvels of the Alliance. Following the devastating loss of Gnomeregan, displaced gnomes dispersed across Alliance lands, bringing their singular knack for tinkering, chemistry, and mechanics with them. In Stormwind City, gnomes found a welcoming sanctuary within the Dwarven District, where blast furnaces and workbenches are plentiful. Sprite Jumpsprocket represents this resilient, forward-looking spirit—determined to master the complex discipline of engineering despite the hardships faced by her kin.

npc:sten-stoutarm.text: Sten Stoutarm. Sten Stoutarm is a practical dwarven outfitter and courier stationed outside Anvilmar in Coldridge Valley. Responsible for keeping new recruits equipped and managing local dispatches, he helps ensure that novice mountaineers stay warm, fed, and informed despite the harsh mountain conditions. Positioned near the heart of Coldridge Valley, Sten Stoutarm is one of the first friendly faces new dwarven and gnomish recruits encounter outside Anvilmar's tavern. With the valley isolated by winter blizzards and encroaching dangers, Sten takes it upon himself to outfit green apprentices with sturdy gear before they freeze or wander unprepared into the drifts. Beyond assembling winter outfitting from local wolf hides, Sten serves as an informal postmaster for Coldridge Valley. He handles messages passed through the treacherous Coldridge Pass and distributes official runes, memoranda, and orders to class trainers throughout the basin, ensuring novice warriors, priests, and mages get their instructions despite the hostile trogg presence blocking the tunnels.

npc:tallonkai-swiftroot.text: Tallonkai Swiftroot. Tallonkai Swiftroot is a night elf resident of Dolanaar in Teldrassil. Concerned with the emerging corruption tainting the great boughs, he enlists young adventurers to recover enchanted relics and stem the foul forces plaguing the woods. Dwelling in the canopy settlement of Dolanaar, Tallonkai Swiftroot keeps a watchful eye over the surrounding woods. Like many night elves living beneath the boughs of the newly grown World Tree, he is alarmed by the unnatural agitation of the wildlife and the unsettling shadows gathering at the edges of their settlements. Tallonkai directs adventurers to confront foul entities disturbing Teldrassil's peace. His concerns include corrupted dream catchers crafted to protect sleeping druids, vicious gnarlpine furbolgs succumbing to a dark malaise, and the corrupted Gnarlpine mystics led by Ferocitas the Dream Eater. To Tallonkai, cleansing these disturbances is crucial to defending the fragile home of the Kaldorei.

npc:verner-osgood.text: Verner Osgood. Verner Osgood is the resident blacksmith of Lakeshire, stationed just outside the town smithy. Balancing local civilian trade with the crushing demands of the Stormwind military, he works tirelessly to keep horses shod and defenders armed amid relentless gnoll raids. Standing by the forge in central Lakeshire, Verner Osgood represents the strained industrial backbone of the Redridge Mountains. Tasked with crafting basic supplies like horseshoes for local mounts, Verner finds his stock constantly co-opted to manufacture weapons and armor for the Stormwind Guard. With the kingdom stretching its borders thin and local garrisons lacking supplies, independent smiths like Verner must carry the logistical burden of the realm's defense. Verner's troubles extend far beyond a shortage of iron. The gnolls infesting the Redridge hills routinely ambush livestock, carrying off working horses whenever they stray outside the town perimeter. Driven to exasperation by the destruction of his livelihood, Verner actively recruits traveling adventurers to cull the marauding packs and hunt down their ferocious packleader, Yowler.

npc:viktori-prism-antras.text: Viktori Prism'Antras. Viktori Prism'Antras is an eccentric stargazer residing in a small hillside hut overlooking Darkshire. While the town around him succumbs to dread and looming horrors, Viktori focuses intently on building a telescope to view the heavens clearly. To realize his vision, he relies on adventurous travelers to acquire intricate parts based on gnomish schematics. Perched up the slope just beyond the gryphon roost, Viktori Prism'Antras spends his days peering outward from the gloom of Duskwood. Amid undead incursions, ravenous spiders, and creeping shadows, his obsession lies far beyond the suffocating canopy. He dreams of building a magnificent optical telescope capable of bringing the stars into brilliant focus, offering a quiet escape from the dread that engulfs the hamlet. Constructing such a delicate apparatus is no simple matter in a cursed forest. Viktori works from blueprints provided by his gnomish friend, Cog Glitzspinner. To complete the device, he enlists passersby to track down rare lens-crafting materials and mechanical housings, ranging from finely cut glass to metal lenses scattered across perilous territory.

npc:william-pestle.text: William Pestle. William Pestle is a human alchemist staying inside Goldshire's Lion's Pride Inn. Together with his brother Morgan, he helps run the apothecary shop in Stormwind's Trade District. He frequently employs traveling adventurers to gather odd reagents like kobold candles, murloc kelp, and herbal supplies. While his brother Morgan Pestle manages the counter at Pestle's Apothecary in the Trade District of Stormwind City, William operates out of the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire. Being stationed in Elwynn Forest allows him to work closely with local gatherers and secure raw materials that city shops constantly require. He maintains regular shipments back to the capital, ensuring Stormwind's citizens have steady access to restorative salves, draughts, and powders. William's craft often demands unusual components that go beyond simple garden herbs. He frequently commissions newcomers to gather wax candles carried by Elwynn's infesting kobolds, as well as crystal kelp taken from the murlocs of Crystal Lake, just east of Goldshire. Although such concoctions seem bizarre to the uninitiated, William insists these strange ingredients possess potent alchemical virtues.

npc:wizbang-cranktoggle.text: Wizbang Cranktoggle. Wizbang Cranktoggle is an eccentric gnome engineer residing on the upper floor of the Auberdine inn. Despite being far from the cog-filled halls of Gnomeregan or Ironforge, he has turned his mechanical ingenuity toward setting up and maintaining automated communication devices known as buzzboxes across the wild coast of Darkshore. While the night elves of Auberdine prefer living in harmony with nature and leaning upon ancient customs, Wizbang Cranktoggle represents the curious, tinkering presence of the Alliance. Perched on the top floor of Auberdine's inn, surrounded by tools and spare components, Wizbang pays little mind to the solemn druidic traditions of Kalimdor, focusing instead on pragmatic mechanical challenges. Wizbang's primary project along Darkshore is deploying and maintaining his peculiar invention: the buzzbox. Designed to establish automated reporting and long-distance communication across the rugged, sprawling coastline, these contraptions often suffer from coastal weathering and the hostility of local wildlife. Wizbang frequently recruits travelers to gather components, salvage tools like gaffer jacks, and recover electropellers to keep his mechanical surveillance functioning.

subzone:alexston-farmstead.text: Alexston Farmstead. The Alexston Farmstead is a derelict farm in Westfall, overgrown and prowled by haywire Harvest Watchers. Once the childhood home of Stormwind's city architect, Baros Alexston, it has fallen into ruin like much of the breadbasket around it. Situated amidst the dry plains of Westfall, the Alexston Farmstead stands as another grim testament to the kingdom's neglect. Like neighboring estates, the farm was abandoned by its caretakers when banditry erupted across the countryside. Today, the fields are overgrown, and the mechanical Harvest Watchers left behind to tend the crops have spun out of control, violently attacking anyone who approaches the barren farmhouse. Despite its bleak state, the farm is tied to one of Stormwind's most prominent citizens. Baros Alexston, the skilled architect who helped design parts of the rebuilt capital, spent his youth toiling on these very fields. He left the farmstead long before the unrest began to pursue his trade in masonry and construction, leaving behind a memento of his early life nestled among the ruins.

subzone:alterac-mountains.text: Alterac Mountains. The Alterac Mountains are a rugged, snow-capped range rising directly above the rolling pastures of Hillsbrad. Once the heart of a proud human kingdom, the slopes now harbor ruined settlements, bandit factions, and dangerous wilderness where travelers rarely walk unguarded. Long before the hills fell into chaos, these highlands formed the sovereign nation of Alterac, one of the seven kingdoms born from ancient Arathor. That legacy shattered during the Second War when King Aiden Perenolde struck a clandestine pact with the Old Horde, allowing orcish forces passage through the peaks in exchange for his kingdom's safety. The Alliance of Lordaeron uncovered the betrayal and deposed Perenolde, leaving the region fractured by martial law and territorial disputes. Following the devastation of the Third War, the mountains collapsed into complete lawlessness. The disinherited nobles of the realm banded together to form the Syndicate, operating out of the ruins of Strahnbrad and plotting to reclaim their lost dominion through sabotage and assassination. Between ruthless Crushridge ogres occupying the shattered capital, marauding gnolls, and the shattered magical ruins around Dalaran, the passes of Alterac remain some of the most perilous pathways in Lordaeron.

subzone:alther-s-mill.text: Alther's Mill. Alther's Mill is a ruined lumber mill tucked into the rugged hills northeast of Lakeshire in the Redridge Mountains. Once a vital source of processed timber for local builders, the abandoned grounds have deteriorated into a haven for feral scavengers and prowling predators. For adventurers traveling east toward Stonewatch, the dilapidated structures serve as a grim landmark marking the boundary of safe frontier territory. Before the region fell prey to invading predators and orc raids, Alther's Mill bustled with timber trade that supplied the construction of Lakeshire and surrounding settlements. Its quiet clearing northeast of Lake Everstill provided ready access to mountain timber stands. As turmoil mounted across the kingdom of Stormwind and the Blackrock clan pushed down from the heights of Stonewatch, local millers abandoned the facility, leaving the dry timber buildings and wheel to decay into rot. In the absence of human workers, the mill became infested with monstrous tarantulas, carrion vultures, and opportunistic raiders. Travelers cutting through the path to the eastern passes must skirt its shadowed perimeter carefully. In recent years, shadowy operatives and thieves have also taken advantage of the abandoned compound, using its discarded storage boxes and hidden corners to hone illicit lockpicking crafts and covert trades far from the eyes of the Lakeshire Town Watch.

subzone:ban-ethil-barrow-den.text: Ban'ethil Barrow Den. Ban'ethil Barrow Den is a sacred subterranean sanctuary hollowed out within the roots of Teldrassil. Originally created as a resting place for the sleeping Druids of the Talon, the cavern complex has recently fallen into chaos. The corrupted furbolgs of the Gnarlpine tribe have overrun its chambers, turning a place of peaceful slumber into a perilous den of madness. Barrow dens serve as sacred resting chambers where night elf druids slumber while projecting their spirits into the Emerald Dream. Ban'ethil Barrow Den was dedicated specifically to sheltering the Druids of the Talon as they communed with nature. Divided into upper and lower subterranean chambers, the den once resonated with tranquil reverie and deep meditative magic. However, the affliction sweeping Teldrassil's wildlife did not spare the Gnarlpine furbolgs, who invaded the complex, turning its hollowed halls into a fortified warren. Driven mad by mysterious corruption taking root across the World Tree, the Gnarlpine tribe drove out or endangered the slumbering druids within Ban'ethil. The furbolgs now fiercely guard the winding tunnels, aggressive toward any night elf who approaches. For the defenders of Teldrassil, reclaiming the barrow den is an urgent priority, not merely to drive back the hostile furbolgs, but to protect the vulnerable druids and sacred relics trapped within its lower depths.

subzone:baradin-bay.text: Baradin Bay. Baradin Bay is the expansive body of water lying between the shores of Khaz Modan, the Wetlands, the Arathi Highlands, and southern Lordaeron. Once vigorously patrolled by the powerful navy of Kul Tiras during the Second War, its waters now conceal treacherous reefs, sunken warships, and hostile aquatic predators. Framed by the coasts of Dun Morogh to the south and Lordaeron to the north, Baradin Bay serves as a vital maritime passage connecting the harbors of the Eastern Kingdoms. The bay is anchored by busy ports like Menethil Harbor in the Wetlands and Southshore in the Hillsbrad Foothills. However, navigating these waters is perilous: shallow sandbanks, jagged shoals, and dangerous fauna like murlocs, crocolisks, and deep-sea sharks pose constant threats to sailors and travelers alike. During the Second War, Baradin Bay witnessed heavy naval conflict as the fleets of Kul Tiras clashed with the Horde. Today, grim reminders of those battles litter the coast and the seabed. The shattered hulls of the Kul Tiran Third Fleet—known locally as the Lost Fleet—rest half-submerged along the Wetlands coast, while other vessels have plummeted down to Drowned Reef. Hostile spirits, opportunistic salvagers, and ravenous sea beasts now haunt the waters surrounding these decaying timber ruins.

subzone:bathran-s-haunt.text: Bathran's Haunt. Bathran's Haunt is an ancient kaldorei ruin nestled in northwestern Ashenvale, east of the Zoram Strand. Recently, Forsaken herbalists and their guardians have overtaken the site to harvest local flora for their alchemical research, steadily withering the surrounding woodland. North of the Ruins of Ordil'Aran, crumbling night elf pillars stand swallowed by thick Ashenvale foliage. What was once a tranquil kaldorei relic has fallen under the shadow of the Forsaken. Skulking among the broken marble, undead herbalists and their enforcers have set up a crude open-air laboratory. Their presence alone blights the ancient soil: grass rots into a sickly brown, vibrant blossoms wilt, and an unnatural decay creeps through the grove as they methodically harvest rare woodland reagents for their experiments. The primary draw of these ruins is Bathran's Hair, a unique remedial herb found taking root only among these particular stones. While night elf and Alliance scouts view the Forsaken presence as a vile desecration of sacred elven soil, the undead work diligently to extract the plant's potent properties. The Horde maintains a vested interest in the compound's botanical yield, though the Forsaken's secretive methods and the resulting corruption of the earth draw suspicion from outsiders and allies alike.

subzone:boulderslide-ravine.text: Boulderslide Ravine. Boulderslide Ravine is a rugged, secluded canyon tucked away in the central peaks of the Stonetalon Mountains, reached via Webwinder Path. Largely spared from the direct clashes between the Horde and Alliance, it serves as the rocky approach to Boulderslide Cavern and remains home to wild mountain beasts. Tucked away off Webwinder Path, Boulderslide Ravine is a narrow cut of rock in the Stonetalon heights. While loggers, night elves, and the Horde battle over timber and sacred glades throughout the region, this craggy pass remains relatively undisturbed by military forces. Wild mountain rams and roaming crag beasts like Cliff Stormers make up the local fauna, navigating the treacherous ledges and sheer stone walls. Prospectors also keep an eye on the ravine, as rich mineral veins frequently crop up along the rocky slopes leading deeper toward the cavern network. Opposite the entrance to Boulderslide Cavern lies a small, quiet cave overlooking the ravine. Lit by rough torches and stacked with weathered supply barrels, the shelter contains primitive tribal paintings across its interior walls. The crude artwork bears a striking resemblance to ancient tauren designs, suggesting that native tribes traveled or sought temporary shelter in these crags long before modern conflict swept into the mountains.

subzone:camp-aparaje.text: Camp Aparaje. Camp Aparaje was once a peaceful tauren village nestled in the eastern heights of the Stonetalon Mountains. Today, it lies overrun and occupied by the hostile Grimtotem tribe, who slaughtered the original settlers and took the outpost for themselves. Perched along the crags of the Stonetalon Mountains, Camp Aparaje was established by peaceful tauren looking to live quietly in the highlands. That tranquility was shattered when raiders from the nearby Grimtotem Post, led by Grundig Darkcloud, launched a brutal and unprovoked assault. The villagers were butchered or driven away, and survivors such as Makaba Flathoof were left mourning the destruction of their home while dreading the fate of captive kin. Now completely occupied by Grimtotem warriors, Camp Aparaje serves as a forward base of operations for the aggressive tribe in the region. Unlike typical Grimtotem settlements that fly blue markings, the great totem standing in Aparaje is carved with deep crimson paint.

subzone:cathedral-square.text: Cathedral Square. Cathedral Square is the spiritual and civic heart of Stormwind City, dominated by the majestic Cathedral of Light. Beyond serving as a place of worship and devotion, the bustling plaza houses municipal institutions like City Hall, the city orphanage, and the regional headquarters of the Argent Dawn. Situated northwest of the Trade District and southeast of the Dwarven District, Cathedral Square serves as the epicenter of faith in the Kingdom of Stormwind. Dominating the skyline is the Cathedral of Light, the preeminent sanctuary for followers of the Holy Light across Azeroth. Priests, paladins, and healers gather here to study, pray, and train. Citizens, pilgrims, and local schoolchildren led by School Mistress Danna regularly mingle in the square for conversation and contemplation. The district is not merely reserved for prayer; it is one of the capital's busiest civic centers. The square houses the Stormwind Orphanage as well as City Hall, anchoring the administrative life of the kingdom. Specialized armorers and weaponsmiths catering to holy crusaders, such as Righteous Plates and Just Maces, line the avenues. It also serves as the base of operations for the Argent Dawn within Stormwind, where recruiters and representatives coordinate relief efforts and rally champions against the encroaching threats of the Scourge in the northern kingdoms.

subzone:cenarion-enclave.text: Cenarion Enclave. The Cenarion Enclave is the verdant northwestern district of Darnassus, serving as the central gathering place and seat of power for the Cenarion Circle in the capital. While Archdruid Malfurion Stormrage lies slumbering within the Emerald Dream, Archdruid Fandral Staghelm leads the night elven druids from the great hollows and living boughs of this grove. Occupying a high terrace above the Temple Gardens, the Cenarion Enclave is shaped from ancient oaks and ashes marked with runic bark. Convocations of the Cenarion Circle gather within structures molded directly from living wood and stone. With Malfurion Stormrage absent in the Emerald Dream, Archdruid Fandral Staghelm oversees affairs here, pushing his ambitious vision for Teldrassil despite lingering political friction with High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind. Beyond the druids who meditate among its streams, the enclave also hosts the capital's elven hunters and the stables where skilled riders learn to tame Darnassian nightsabers. Though renowned as a tranquil sanctuary of nature, the enclave harbors more covert activities. Beneath the hollowed roots of the westernmost bough lies a subterranean refuge used by Darnassus's clandestine rogues, who conduct their quiet business shielded by the rustling canopy above.

subzone:charred-vale.text: Charred Vale. The Charred Vale is a smoldering valley in southwestern Stonetalon Mountains, devastated by the reckless deforestation and machinery of the Venture Company. Once a thriving haven for treants and chimaeras, it is now engulfed in flames, roving elementals, and hostile harpies. Not long ago, this southwest basin was a flourishing alpine wood guarded by majestic treants and inhabited by native chimaeras and harpies. Its ruin began with the arrival of the Venture Company. The greedy goblin outfit clear-cut the forest with explosive machinery, corrupting the guardians and awakening chaotic fire elementals. Though the treants eventually forced the goblins back, the land was left broken, scarred by fire, and tainted by whatever foul devices the retreating loggers deployed. Today, blackened ancients wander blindly through smoke and ash alongside enraged elementals. Bloodfury harpies roost in the skeletal snags, defending what remains of their territory. Despite the hostility of the valley, druids from Sun Rock Retreat refuse to abandon the region, dispatching travelers to sow enchanted seeds and tend the corrupted ancients in a persistent campaign to reclaim the scorched earth.

subzone:clean-zone.text: Clean Zone. The Clean Zone is a fortified, decontamination enclave nestled inside the ruined city of Gnomeregan just past the upper Hall of Gears. It serves as the sole safe haven within the irradiated facility where uncorrupted gnomish forces hold ground against surrounding troggs and leper gnomes. Here, field medics, technicians, and specialized Sparklematic machines offer respite and salvage operations amid the radioactive ruins. While most of Gnomeregan succumbed to Mekkatorque's disastrous venting of radioactive waste, the Clean Zone remains untainted. Positioned strategically between the trogg-infested Dormitory below and the contested corridors of the Hall of Gears above, it acts as a fortified forward base. Resolute gnome defenders, technicians, and field medics hold the barricades day and night, ensuring Alliance expeditions have a stable staging ground to regroup, mend wounds, and maintain machinery. Beyond serving as a military redoubt, the Clean Zone is a hub for salvaging the lost capital. Gnomish engineers installed Sparklematic 5200 units to chemically scrub and wash grime-encrusted relics hauled out of the city's radioactive underbelly. Technicians and merchants like Tink Sprocketwhistle process these reclaimed gears and baubles, outfitting adventurers while studying the lingering toxic fallout that plagues the deep tunnels.

subzone:cleft.text: Cleft. The Cleft is a darkened hollow located northwest of Dolanaar in Teldrassil. Once a tranquil corner of the boughs, it has been claimed by the corrupted Gnarlpine furbolgs, who use it as a stronghold to ambush travelers moving along the main highway toward Darnassus. Situated off the highway between Dolanaar and Darnassus, the Cleft has turned into one of the most perilous dens on the world tree. Driven mad by the foul taint spreading through Teldrassil, the resident Gnarlpine furbolgs have fortified this hollow. From this redoubt, the maddened beasts terrorize the local roads, threatening to cut Dolanaar off from the capital.

subzone:command-center.text: Command Center. The Command Center, often referred to as the Stormwind Barracks, stands in the heart of Old Town as the operational headquarters for the city's military officers. In peacetime, it houses the standing army, but with Stormwind's forces dispatched to distant frontiers, it currently operates with a seasoned skeleton crew focused on drilling recruits and local militia.
