Situated within the weathered streets of Old Town, the Command Center serves as the primary garrison and martial training ground for the kingdom of Stormwind. Normally packed with regular infantry and ranking officers, the facility is uncharacteristically sparse. With much of the royal army committed to campaigns abroad, the barracks relies on a veteran cadre of instructors—including Ander Germaine and martial artist Wu Shen—to train fresh warriors to bolster the city's defenses. Guards throughout Stormwind often direct newcomers to the 'Barracks' when seeking instruction in heavy arms and tactical combat. The building's proximity to both the Pig and Whistle Tavern and the shadowy operations elsewhere in Old Town makes it an essential anchor of order in a district known for tavern brawls and roguish activity.

subzone:craftsmen-s-terrace.text: Craftsmen's Terrace. The Craftsmen's Terrace is the bustling artisan district situated in the northern reaches of Darnassus. It serves as the primary trade and manufacturing hub for the night elf capital, housing workshops, profession trainers, and a lively inn. The district also hosts external representatives, including an embassy for the neutral Argent Dawn. Spanning the northern edge of the canopy city, the Craftsmen's Terrace gathers the diverse trades that keep Darnassus running. Woodworkers, leathercrafters, alchemists, and other artisans operate their shops here, integrating classic night elven methods with practical craft. The district also provides essential community amenities, including an inn, a guild master, and guild petition vendors. Bridges connect the terrace directly to the Cenarion Enclave to the west and the Warrior's Terrace to the south. Despite the kaldorei's historic isolation, the Craftsmen's Terrace is home to foreign connections, most notably an embassy established by the Argent Dawn to coordinate with northern allies against the Scourge. Visitors browsing the district's various workshops might also stumble across scattered scholarly volumes, ranging from historical accounts of the War of the Ancients to chronicles detailing the Second War and esoteric treatises on the Old Gods.

subzone:cragpool-lake.text: Cragpool Lake. Cragpool Lake is a body of water tucked inside Windshear Crag in the Stonetalon Mountains. Looming above its dark waters sits a massive timber structure erected by the Venture Company. Nestled within Windshear Crag, Cragpool Lake lies directly beneath the towering logging apparatus built by the Venture Company. An enormous wooden structure spans above the water, serving as the vantage point from which Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle oversees operations across the mountain valley. Venture Company workers occupy the platforms overhead.

subzone:dagger-hills.text: Dagger Hills. The Dagger Hills form a rugged ridge rising across southern Westfall, directly behind the blighted town of Moonbrook. Long neglected by the crown, this rocky highland serves as a hostile hideout for cutthroats, bandits, and creeping terrors that threaten the surrounding plains. Rising high above the dilapidated settlement of Moonbrook, the Dagger Hills mark the jagged southern reaches of Westfall. Stripped of official royal patrols from Stormwind, this arid highland has become a natural fortification for the Defias Brotherhood. Knuckledusters, pathstalkers, and highwaymen lurk among the rocky crests and scrub, ambushing unwary travelers and keeping watch over the approaches to their strongholds below. Beyond mortal outlaws, the Dagger Hills carry an eerie reputation under cover of darkness. The unsettling specter Leprithus, a wandering ghoul, has been sighted stalking the desolate heights when the sun dips. Aside from wandering outlaws and lingering undead, the only resident willing to brave the ridge is Grimbooze Thunderbrew, a dwarven brewer who sets up his distilling equipment in the rugged wilderness regardless of the nearby dangers.

subzone:demon-fall-canyon.text: Demon Fall Canyon. Demon Fall Canyon is a scarred, fel-corrupted gorge situated in southern Ashenvale. It marks the legendary battleground where Grommash Hellscream and Thrall confronted the pit lord Mannoroth, ending the demonic blood curse that had enslaved the orcish race for a generation. Carved into the rugged southern borders of Ashenvale near Felfire Hill and Demon Fall Ridge, this canyon bears the heavy scars of the Third War. It was here that Warchief Thrall and chieftain Grommash Hellscream tracked down the pit lord Mannoroth to break his hold over the Horde. During the fierce duel, Mannoroth incapacitated Thrall, but Grom seized the opening to drive his axe, Gorehowl, straight into the demon's chest. The resulting infernal explosion shattered the pit lord and slew Grom as well, permanently liberating the orcs from their lingering demonic servitude. Following Mannoroth's demise, the Horde dubbed the canyon to commemorate Grom's final stand, erecting a monument nearby to honor his redemption. Despite the pit lord's destruction, his violent death unleashed raw demonic power that thoroughly tainted the surrounding land. Today, the canyon remains saturated in fel magic and crawls with hostile lingering lesser demons, making any pilgrimage to this hallowed ground a perilous venture.

subzone:demon-fall-ridge.text: Demon Fall Ridge. Demon Fall Ridge is a blighted highland in south-eastern Ashenvale, overlooking the canyon where Mannoroth fell. Swarming with lesser demons and corrupting magic, the ridge centers around a desecrated night elf barrow den claimed by the Burning Legion. Rising directly west and above Demon Fall Canyon, Demon Fall Ridge is stained with lingering fel residue from the Third War. While the canyon below marks the site of the catastrophic clash between Grommash Hellscream and the pit lord Mannoroth, this high ground serves as a staging area for surviving demonic invaders. Lesser demons patrol the rocky cliffs, defiling the ancient woodland and threatening any travelers traversing the southern border of Ashenvale. Carved into the side of the ridge rests an abandoned night elf barrow den, hollowed out and converted into a stronghold of dark sorcery. Rather than slumbering druids, the subterranean passages teem with fel fiends. Deep in the subterranean depths lurks Diathorus the Seeker, a cunning dreadlord who rules over this conclave, directing the remaining demonic remnants throughout the forest.

subzone:dormitory.text: Dormitory. The Dormitory is a residential sector within the fallen technological capital of Gnomeregan. Once providing living quarters for countless gnome citizens, it now lies choked with radioactive fallout and crawls with savage, irradiated troggs. Situated just past the decontamination chambers of the Clean Zone, the Dormitory formerly housed the inventors, laborers, and families of Gnomeregan. When High Tinker Mekkatorque initiated the emergency radiation venting to combat the invading trogg horde, this densely populated sector became a trap. Today, its communal halls and living units are completely abandoned by gnomish life, occupied instead by mutated troggs that thrive in the radioactive miasma. Travelers descending toward the lower levels of the city must fight through this tragic reminder of the catastrophe to reach the lower Hall of Gears. Amid the abandoned living quarters, remnants of the city's administrative apparatus still function. The Matrix Punchograph 3005-B machines process security punch cards. These terminals provide clearance for higher-security data terminals deeper within Gnomeregan, helping recover important records left behind when the gnomes fled.

subzone:dun-garok.text: Dun Garok. Dun Garok is a fortified dwarven mountain bastion situated in the southeastern heights of the Hillsbrad Foothills. Commanded by Captain Ironhill, the outpost's stalwart garrison defends regional Alliance interests and nearby operations like the Azurelode Mine against hostile encroachment. To the Forsaken of Tarren Mill, this entrenched dwarven stronghold stands as a constant military threat bordering their domain. Carved into the craggy southeastern hills of Hillsbrad Foothills, Dun Garok stands as a heavily defended redoubt of Ironforge mountaineers and riflemen. Commanded by Captain Ironhill, the dwarves here maintain a critical defensive perimeter, shielding human settlements in Hillsbrad and securing vital operations at the Azurelode Mine. Their sturdy stone architecture and deep entrenchments provide the Alliance with an anchor against nearby threats. Because of its close proximity to Tarren Mill, Dun Garok is viewed by the Forsaken as an intolerable intrusion on their southern border. Sylvanas Windrunner's forces loathe the presence of heavily armed dwarven troops so close to their stronghold, routinely plotting to infiltrate the fortress, break its defenses, and eliminate Captain Ironhill's garrison to secure Forsaken dominion over Hillsbrad.

subzone:dun-modr.text: Dun Modr. Dun Modr is an ancient fortified dwarven town in northern Wetlands, guarding the southern approach to the Thandol Span. Once a critical fortress held and contested across multiple wars, it has recently fallen to a hostile force of Dark Iron dwarves. Situated at the northern edge of the Wetlands, Dun Modr commands the primary overland highway linking Khaz Modan with the northern human kingdoms. Because of this vital location, the stronghold has seen heavy bloodshed over the decades. During the Second War, the Orcish Horde captured and entrenched themselves within the dwarven fortress, using it as a forward staging ground to launch raids and repel Alliance armies. Stromgarde warriors launched a brutal amphibious assault from Tol Barad to reclaim it, only for the Orcs to strike back in a bloody tug-of-war. Alliance forces led by Lord Anduin Lothar ultimately drove the invaders south across the Thandol Span, restoring dwarven custody over the bastion. With Ironforge's attention divided and many of its finest mountaineers committed to Alliance duties abroad, Dun Modr was left vulnerable. Seizing the opportunity, Dark Iron invaders pushed north and sabotaged the Thandol Span with explosives before swarming the fortress. Under the command of the Dark Iron warlock Balgaras the Foul, these infiltrators overran the town's defenders, driving out the Bronzebeard garrison and transforming the strategic outpost into a hostile den. Surrounding Mountaineers now maintain a grim perimeter just down the road, desperately seeking aid to dislodge the occupiers.

subzone:durnholde-keep.text: Durnholde Keep. Durnholde Keep is a shattered fortress situated east of Tarren Mill in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Once the nerve center of the Alliance's orc internment camps and the place where Warchief Thrall was raised as a captive gladiator, it now lies in ruin, occupied by outlaws of the Syndicate. Built by the Alliance, Durnholde served as the headquarters overseeing the southern internment camps following the Second War. Commanded by the ambitious and corrupt Lieutenant General Aedelas Blackmoore, it functioned as both an administrative fortress and a gladiatorial arena. It was here that Blackmoore raised the orphaned infant Go'el, naming him Thrall and training him to fight for sport and profit. Aided by Taretha Foxton, Thrall escaped captivity and later united the dispersed orc clans under the banner of the new Horde. Returning to Durnholde, Thrall laid siege to the fortress, slew Blackmoore, and called upon the earth spirits to shatter its walls. Since its collapse prior to the Third War, Durnholde Keep has remained a scarred heap of masonry. In the vacuum left by Lordaeron's fall, the aristocratic bandits of the Syndicate took refuge among the ramparts. Operating out of the broken bailey and towers, these dispossessed Alterac nobles and cutthroats prey upon travelers across the Hillsbrad Foothills, turning a former instrument of martial law into a heavily fortified rogue outpost.

subzone:echo-ridge-mine.text: Echo Ridge Mine. Echo Ridge Mine is a small excavation carved into the northwestern cliffs of Northshire Valley. Rich in stone and ore, it has recently fallen into the clutches of a destructive kobold infestation, halting Northshire's local operations. Tucked away in the hills above Northshire Abbey, Echo Ridge Mine was meant to supply the valley with useful stone and metal. Instead, opportunistic kobolds swarmed through the tunnels, driving out the local workers. Marshal McBride views the infestation as an unacceptable security risk to Northshire's safety and recruitment efforts, directing new recruits straight into the tunnels to cull their numbers and reclaim the site. The occupation of Echo Ridge is part of a broader pattern of kobold encroachment spreading across Elwynn Forest. If left unchecked in the northwestern ridge, these subterranean pests threaten to disrupt Northshire's peaceful training grounds and choke off crucial resources from reaching the abbey.

subzone:engineering-labs.text: Engineering Labs. The Engineering Labs are a multi-tiered research and manufacturing facility deep within Gnomeregan. Connected to the Workshop Entrance and Launch Bay, this bustling center of gnome innovation was overrun during the city's radioactive cataclysm and is now swarming with crazed leper gnomes and rogue mechanical contraptions. Built around a central mechanical structure, the Engineering Labs span two primary tiers connected by a central cargo lift. In Gnomeregan's prime, tinkerers here developed schematics and fine-tuned clockwork inventions. Today, radiation leaks have driven the remaining researchers mad, transforming them into deranged leper gnomes who mindlessly guard malfunctioning machinery alongside rogue constructs. Beyond its historical role as a laboratory, the chamber serves as a vital transit hub through the lower reaches of the ruined city. Passages wind toward the Launch Bay, Tinkers' Court, and the Workshop Entrance back door. The lower floor also houses the Matrix Punchograph 3005-D terminals, critical processing units required to decipher the coded punch cards carried by gnome engineers.

subzone:falfarren-river.text: Falfarren River. The Falfarren River flows northeast to southwest through the heart of Ashenvale, originating on the slopes of Mount Hyjal before slipping underground beneath the Barrens' northern mountains. It forms a natural boundary between night elven domains around Astranaar to the west and the encroaching Horde outposts to the east. Travelers must tread carefully, as its shaded banks and shallows harbor hostile wildlife and mark the edge of open conflict. Feeding down from Mount Hyjal, the waters of the Falfarren cascade across waterfalls into Xavian before winding between Splintertree Post and Night Run. While it is neither exceptionally deep nor impassable under ordinary weather, it serves as the rough geopolitical dividing line in central Ashenvale. To the west lie Astranaar and the core holdings of the Kaldorei; to the east sit the camps and lumber operations of the Horde. Crossing the main road's wooden bridges brings travelers into the contested heart of the forest, where patrols clash along the banks. Beyond the tensions of warring sentinels and grunts, the river conceals natural and unnatural dangers beneath its surface. Downstream near Felfire Hill, corrupted bog beasts and aggressive water creatures prowl the muddy shallows. Rainfall can swell the currents, yet the true peril lies in the dense canopies flanking either shore, where ambushes and skirmishes routinely spill into the stream.

subzone:farstrider-lodge.text: Farstrider Lodge. Farstrider Lodge is a hunting outpost in southeastern Loch Modan. Its architecture appears to be high elven, while its residents include the high elf Vyrin Swiftwind, dwarves, and humans. Hunters and travelers come here for training, supplies, and work in the surrounding wilds. Farstrider Lodge stands apart from the sturdy stone buildings typical of Khaz Modan. Its architecture suggests high elven craftsmanship. Vyrin Swiftwind is the only known high elf still residing here, alongside dwarves and humans. The lodge's founder and date of construction are not established. Situated in the southeastern hills of Loch Modan, the lodge serves hunters and travelers exploring the surrounding wilderness. Hunter and pet trainers work here alongside merchants and people seeking help with local wildlife.

subzone:fel-rock.text: Fel Rock. Fel Rock is a blighted cavern hidden within the woods just north of Dolanaar on the boughs of Teldrassil. Once a tranquil hollow, it has fallen into corruption under the influence of the satyr Lord Melenas and his horde of vicious grells. Tucked away in the forested hills north of Dolanaar, Fel Rock was once an ordinary, peaceful cavern carved into the wood and stone of Teldrassil. Today, it stands as an unsettling reminder of the creeping taint encroaching on the world tree. Twisted roots and unnatural shadows dominate the cavern interior, overrun by swarms of wild grells and grellkin. The corruption within Fel Rock stems from the presence of Lord Melenas, a wicked satyr who has claimed the hollow as a stronghold. From deep within the cave, he orchestrates the spread of malevolent corruption right under the watchful gaze of the night elf sentinels. Druids from Dolanaar, particularly Tallonkai Swiftroot, actively enlist capable defenders to cleanse the cave and slay Melenas before his foul blight can spread further into the surrounding woodlands.

subzone:felfire-hill.text: Felfire Hill. Felfire Hill is a blighted, demon-infested rise nestled in eastern Ashenvale. Struck by falling infernals during the Third War, its corrupted soil still burns with demonic power. The Horde maintains fortified guard posts on the bridges leading into the hill to safeguard their nearby settlements. During the cataclysmic invasion of the Third War, flaming meteors fell across Kalimdor as the Burning Legion unleashed its dread infernals. Several of those fiery behemoths struck this ridge in Ashenvale, scouring away the ancient woodlands and corrupting the earth itself. Today, the scorched landscape remains saturated with fel energy and prowled by lingering demons who survived the Legion's defeat at Mount Hyjal. Situated southeast of Splintertree Post and southwest of the Warsong Lumber Camp, Felfire Hill sits uncomfortably close to vital Horde operations. Because the demonic remnants threaten to spill out into the surrounding forest, Horde forces have erected fortified barricades and guard towers at both bridges approaching the hill, containing the foul creatures within their blighted haven.

subzone:fire-scar-shrine.text: Fire Scar Shrine. Fire Scar Shrine is a despoiled night elf shrine nestled in the southwestern forests of Ashenvale. Once a serene place of worship, it has been corrupted by demonic forces and turned into a blister of fel energy right on Astranaar's doorstep. Located southwest of Astranaar and west of the Ruins of Stardust, Fire Scar Shrine stands as a grim reminder of the Burning Legion's lingering poison in Ashenvale. The shrine has fallen under the sway of demonic corruption, nurtured by servants of the shadowy Cult of the Dark Strand and the Shadow Council. Fel magic has twisted the surrounding earth into scorched rock, where roaming demons now gather in open defiance of the forest's defenders. The shrine's descent into darkness was spearheaded by agents like the orcish warlock Ilkrud Magthrull, operating under the orders of Athrikus Narassin. Though mortal sorcerers brought the corruption to bear, summoned fiends now patrol the altar stones unchecked. The localized tear in the veil occasionally draws greater horrors, including the towering doomguard Akkrilus.

subzone:forest-s-edge.text: Forest's Edge. Forest's Edge is a wooded wedge of land along the southwestern frontier of Elwynn Forest, flanked by rivers leading toward Westfall. Guarded to the north by Westbrook Garrison, this untamed area has become dangerously overrun by riverpaw gnolls under the command of the notorious Hogger. Tucked southwest of Stormwind City between Mirror Lake Orchard and the rivers bordering Westfall, Forest's Edge forms a natural peninsula of woodland. Despite its proximity to Westbrook Garrison, the Stormwind army's thin ranks have left the area vulnerable to wild beasts and raiding parties. Wandering boars roam among the trees and along the riverbanks, but the true menace is the concentration of Riverpaw gnolls who have made these woods their staging ground. The woods of Forest's Edge are the hunting grounds of Hogger, a massive and brutal gnoll chieftain. With a sizable bounty placed on his head by the Stormwind Army, Hogger directs his pack in harassing travelers and raiding nearby farms, turning what could be a peaceful timberland into a lethal proving ground for young Alliance adventurers.

subzone:forest-song.text: Forest Song. Forest Song is an ancient night elf ruin nestled in northeastern Ashenvale, near the tainted woods of Satyrnaar and the great portal at Bough Shadow. At present, it stands largely deserted save for the vigilant druid Kayneth Stillwind, who watches over the eastern border against emergent threats. Tucked away in the dense woodlands of northeastern Ashenvale, Forest Song was once an elegant settlement of the kaldorei. Today, white stone columns and crumbling archways are overgrown with ivy and wild ferns. Located northeast of Satyrnaar and just north of the encroaching Warsong Lumber Camp, the ruins hold a quiet, strategic overlook along the eastern trails toward Azshara and Bough Shadow. While the woods around it are plagued by demonic corruption and Horde incursions, the ruin itself maintains a haunting, tranquil stillness. Forest Song is currently manned solely by the druid Kayneth Stillwind. From this crumbling outpost, Stillwind keeps a watchful eye on the dark designs of enemies entering the wilderness, including the unsettling presence of the Forsaken in the eastern forests. Though isolated far from Astranaar and lacking garrison fortifications, the sanctuary serves as an important rallying point for Alliance travelers venturing toward the northern road into Felwood or investigating the corruptions seeping across the canopy.

subzone:forlorn-cavern.text: Forlorn Cavern. Tucked along the northern shores of Ironforge's subterranean lake, the Forlorn Cavern is a dimly lit, secluded district far removed from the city's bustling Great Forge. It serves as a shadowy refuge where thieves, cutpurses, and practitioners of the dark arts conduct their business away from prying dwarven guards. While the rest of Ironforge clangs with anvil strikes and radiates heat from the Great Forge, the Forlorn Cavern is cold, damp, and hushed. Wrapping along the northern edge of the mountain's underground lake, the winding pathways sit comfortably out of sight between the Mystic Ward and the Hall of Explorers. Its gloom makes it an ideal gathering place for those who prefer to keep their affairs discreet. Rogues and warlocks train here alongside vendors serving them, while weapon merchants and fishermen also work beside the lake.

subzone:frostmane-hold.text: Frostmane Hold. Frostmane Hold is a fortified encampment and cavern complex claimed by the Frostmane ice trolls in western Dun Morogh. Tucked into the crags south of Gnomeregan, it serves as a central staging ground for troll raiders encroaching on dwarven territory. The Ironforge Guard keeps a close watch on the hold to gauge the growing troll threat. Carved into the freezing cliffs of western Dun Morogh, Frostmane Hold consists of rough outdoor structures and a winding cave system. For the Frostmane tribe, it functions as a primary stronghold, densely guarded by hideskinners and headhunters. From here, the trolls launch raids into the surrounding valleys, testing the defenses of nearby settlements like Kharanos and menacing travelers along the mountain passes. As tensions in Dun Morogh mount, dwarven commanders in Kharanos have grown increasingly concerned about the scale of the Frostmane buildup. Young mountaineers and adventurers are routinely dispatched to scout the interior caverns, map out the defenses, and cull the warbands before the tribe can muster an organized assault against dwarven outposts.

subzone:furlbrow-s-pumpkin-farm.text: Furlbrow's Pumpkin Farm. Furlbrow's Pumpkin Farm is an overrun homestead in northern Westfall, just off the main road from Elwynn Forest. Once a prosperous plot tended by Farmer Furlbrow and his wife Verna, the fields and farmhouse have been seized by the Defias Brotherhood and prowling harvest golems. Situated near the northern border of Westfall, Furlbrow's Pumpkin Farm was once known for producing robust crops to feed the kingdom. That ended when the Defias Brotherhood swept across the countryside. Outlaws drove Farmer Furlbrow and his wife Verna from their land, leaving their fields overrun with mechanical harvest golems programmed to attack anyone approaching. With the farm buildings occupied by bandits and the fields prowled by renegade machinery, the rightful owners have been forced to camp along the roadside near the Jansen Stead, mourning the loss of their home and livelihood. The farm's fall illustrates the broader collapse of law and order across Westfall. With Stormwind's military garrison spread thin and unable to safeguard rural freeholders, the Defias Brotherhood easily claimed homesteads like Furlbrow's. Bandits use the property as an staging ground and camp while letting lethal harvest watchers guard the perimeter, leaving travelers on the nearby highway vulnerable to ambush.

subzone:goblin-foundry.text: Goblin Foundry. The Goblin Foundry is an industrial workshop deep within the Deadmines where goblin tinkerers manufacture heavy metalwork for the Defias Brotherhood. A massive smelting cauldron dominates the chamber, which remains occupied by goblin craftsmen and engineers under Gilnid. Carved into the subterranean depths of Moonbrook, the Goblin Foundry provides the Defias Brotherhood with heavy manufacturing power. Goblin craftsmen and engineers work among the smelters and iron ramps, producing anchors and cannonballs. Gilnid presides over the foundry's goblin workforce. Craftsmen maintain production while engineers defend the workshop with remote-controlled golems, making its narrow ramps and molten metal dangerous for intruders.

subzone:gol-bolar-quarry-mine.text: Gol'Bolar Quarry Mine. Gol'Bolar Quarry Mine is an overrun excavation pit deep within the heart of Gol'Bolar Quarry in eastern Dun Morogh. Originally worked by dwarven miners, the tunnels breached subterranean trogg caverns, unleashing a violent infestation that claimed the entire site. Today, the deepest shafts serve as the stronghold for the trogg warband led by the brute Hammerspine. The mine was established by Ironforge dwarves seeking stone and rich ore deposits beneath the craggy peaks of Dun Morogh. Work came to an abrupt, violent halt when pickaxes fractured a wall into an ancient subterranean cavern system inhabited by troggs. Swarming out from the dark, the subterranean beasts overwhelmed the work crews and forced a hasty retreat, ultimately spilling outward to overrun the surrounding quarry pit as well. While younger, weaker troggs roam the sunlit terraces of the quarry basin, the mine itself harbors the warband's fiercest fighters. Deep within these cramped, torchlit tunnels lurks their vicious chieftain, Hammerspine. Reclaiming the valuable quarry remains an urgent priority for the local mountaineers, but driving the infestation out requires venturing into the blackest depths of the mine to cut off the beasts at their source.

subzone:great-forge.text: Great Forge. The Great Forge is the fiery heart and namesake of the dwarven capital of Ironforge. Situated at the very center of the city, its massive furnaces and famed Great Anvil never rest, producing legendary armaments and serving as the bustling center of civic life. The Great Forge was the very first structure built by the early dwarves beneath Ironforge Mountain, and the grand capital grew in concentric rings around it. Molten stone and slag pour constantly from giant foundries into glowing channels, illuminating the cavern with an amber haze. At its center stands the massive Great Anvil, overseen by Master of the Forge Myolor Sunderfury. Renowned masters of metalwork gather around its rim, hammering out armor, tools, and weapons day and night. Beyond its smithing operations, the Great Forge is the bustling crossroads of the entire mountain city. Ringed with guild offices, supply shops, and the city's primary gryphon roost maintained by Gryth Thurden, travelers from every corner of the Alliance mingle amid the clatter of hammers.

subzone:great-lift.text: Great Lift. The Great Lift is a massive, tauren-engineered elevator system perched on the southern edge of the Barrens. It serves as the primary route lowering travelers and supplies hundreds of feet into the sheer canyon basin of Thousand Needles. Despite its strategic value, aggressive quilboar encroaching through the southern wastes have made approaching the rim increasingly perilous. Spanning the sheer cliff edge between the southern Barrens and the canyon floor of Thousand Needles, the Great Lift stands as a marvel of practical tauren construction. Built using heavy timber, braided rope, and counterweighted pulleys, its paired platforms carry caravans, couriers, and warriors safely across a vertical precipice that would otherwise break any wagon. At the top and bottom platforms, tauren like Brave Moonhorn and Grish Longrunner maintain watch, keeping travelers informed of the road ahead and ensuring cargo passes smoothly. Operating the lift has become increasingly hazardous due to the hostile territory above it. Aggressive quilboar tribes in the southern Barrens have expanded aggressively southward, choking the road toward the lift and threatening to cut off Thousand Needles from the northern trails entirely. Those who make the long journey south must constantly fend off razorfen raiders before they can ever step foot onto the wooden platforms.

subzone:greatwood-vale.text: Greatwood Vale. Greatwood Vale is a forested valley nestled in the eastern foothills of the Stonetalon Mountains, reached via the perilous Webwinder Path. Recently, the hostile Grimtotem tribe seized the vale, using it as a staging ground for bloody assaults on neighboring settlements. Tucked away off the Webwinder Path, Greatwood Vale has become a violent frontier. The Grimtotem tribe, under the ruthless leadership of Grundig Darkcloud, has moved into the vale in force, cutting off safe passage and bringing terror to the surrounding foothills. The Grimtotem did not merely occupy Greatwood Vale; they used it to orchestrate the butchery of nearby Camp Aparaje. Sweeping out of the woods, Darkcloud's raiders slaughtered nearly every tauren inhabiting the encampment. Makaba Flathoof, one of the few survivors who managed to flee the carnage, now directs vengeful Horde warriors straight into the heart of Greatwood Vale to cut down the renegade Grimtotem and put an end to Grundig Darkcloud.

subzone:greenpaw-village.text: Greenpaw Village. Greenpaw Village is a furbolg settlement nestled in central Ashenvale, situated between Raynewood Retreat and Silverwind Refuge. It serves as the primary home of the Foulweald tribe, led by Chief Murgut and the shaman Oakpaw. Gripped by demonic corruption and embattled by outside forces, the village is an active conflict point for both Alliance and Horde travelers. Situated south of Raynewood Retreat and northeast of Silverwind Refuge, Greenpaw Village was once a quiet home for the forest's ursine denizens. In the wake of the Third War, its resident furbolgs—the Foulweald tribe—succumbed to the insidious corruption tainting Ashenvale's soil and spirits. Under the dominion of Chief Murgut and their corrupted spiritual guide, Shaman Oakpaw, the Foulweald have become hostile and unstable, attacking any travelers who stray into their forest territory. Because of their relentless aggression and proximity to major roadways, Greenpaw Village draws hostility from every side. Alliance sentinels and night elf druids seek to purge the mad furbolgs to protect their nearby outposts and sacred moonwells. Simultaneously, Horde forces advancing into Ashenvale have fought bloody skirmishes against the Foulweald as both factions push through the ancient woodland.

subzone:grim-batol.text: Grim Batol. Grim Batol is an ancient, ruined dwarven mountain fortress looming over the eastern edge of the Wetlands. Built by the Wildhammer clan, abandoned after a dark curse during the War of the Three Hammers, and later occupied by the Dragonmaw orcs as a dragon breeding lair, its sealed gates remain an ominous blight upon the highlands. Following the ancient civil war of the three clans, Thane Khardros Wildhammer carved Grim Batol out of the jagged mountains east of the marsh. During the subsequent War of the Three Hammers, the Dark Iron sorceress Modgud laid siege to the fortress. Although Khardros struck her down, Modgud cast a foul shadow across the stones before her death. The lingering taint rendered the halls uninhabitable, forcing the surviving Wildhammer dwarves to abandon their magnificent kingdom and migrate north into the Hinterlands. Centuries later during the Second War, the fortress found a darker purpose when Orgrim Doomhammer dispatched the Dragonmaw clan to claim it. Led by the warlock Nekros Skullcrusher, the orcs utilized the ancient artifact known as the Demon Soul to enslave the red Dragonqueen Alexstrasza deep within the mountain's roots. Forced to hatch broods for the Horde's war effort, Alexstrasza remained chained until a small band of heroes shattered the artifact. Once freed, the enraged Dragon Aspect incinerated the orcs within, leaving Grim Batol a smoldering, desolate ruin watched closely by surviving red dragons.

subzone:grizzled-den.text: Grizzled Den. The Grizzled Den is a cavern nestled in the snowy hills just southwest of Kharanos. It serves as a notorious lair for the ferocious, frost-breathing wendigos indigenous to Dun Morogh. Carved deep into the crags southwest of Kharanos, the Grizzled Den is notorious among local mountaineers as the nesting ground of Dun Morogh's wendigo packs. These aggressive, ape-like beasts wield frosty breath against intruders and band together to protect their hollows. Despite the peril, daring hunters regularly brave the cavern's depths to harvest thick wendigo manes, which fetch a respectable sum among craftsmen looking to line cold chairs and carriage seats with insulated fur. Beyond its fearsome inhabitants, the twisting tunnels of the Grizzled Den draw opportunists searching for natural wealth. Prospectors frequently venture past the outer entrance to hammer at copper veins jutting from the frozen stone walls, while adventurous scouts often scour the darker corners for discarded footlockers. However, delve too far into the inner reaches, and you are bound to face the dens' largest and most vicious predators lurking in the shadows.

subzone:grove-of-the-ancients.text: Grove of the Ancients. The Grove of the Ancients is a sacred night elven sanctuary set amidst old temple ruins in southeastern Darkshore. Nestled beside the Wildbend River, this serene haven serves as a gathering ground for nature spirits and is watched over by the venerable Ancient of Lore, Onu. Tucked away near the southeastern mountains of Darkshore, the Grove of the Ancients stands as a peaceful haven surrounded by aged temple stones. Through its heart flows the surging Wildbend River, providing a quiet refuge amidst a coastline increasingly plagued by corruption and restless wildlife. The grove serves as a meeting place for the Circle of Ancients, where nature spirits and kaldorei tend to the delicate balance of the forest. The focal presence within the grove is Onu, a towering Ancient of Lore who observes the land's shifting fortunes and offers ancient wisdom to passing travelers. Alongside Onu, wandering merchants and slumbering druids find rest beneath the boughs. Though quiet, the grove lies close to territorial furbolg camps to the southeast, making it an essential frontier outpost for Alliance sentinels and druids monitoring southern Darkshore.

subzone:gryphon-roost.text: Gryphon Roost. Perched along the ramparts just east of Stormwind's Trade District, the Gryphon Roost serves as the capital's primary transit hub for aerial travel. Managed by the human gryphon master Dungar Longdrink, it houses the majestic beasts that ferry couriers, soldiers, and adventurers across the Eastern Kingdoms. Situated atop the fortifications overlooking the Trade District canal, the Gryphon Roost connects the capital with outlying Alliance garrisons and settlements throughout the Eastern Kingdoms. The flight network is orchestrated by the seasoned master Dungar Longdrink, who coordinates routes to Ironforge, Lakeshire, Sentinel Hill, and beyond. While Stormwind is predominantly a kingdom of men, the presence of gryphons and their handlers brings a bit of Hinterlands tradition directly into the city walls. Gryphons have long been revered partners of the Wildhammer clan, who introduced aerial warfare and transport to the broader Alliance during the Second War. Here on the roost, the salty smell of leather, feed, and fresh winds creates a distinct frontier atmosphere amid the city's stone masonry.

subzone:hall-of-arms-northshire.text: Hall of Arms (Northshire). The Hall of Arms is the martial wing of Northshire Abbey, situated south of the Main Hall. Here, veteran instructors drill the newest recruits of the Stormwind Army in the arts of the sword, shield, and holy combat. While the clerics and scholars ponder ancient tomes across the courtyard in the Library Wing, the Hall of Arms rings with the clash of blunted steel and the heavy cadence of martial instruction. Positioned on the south side of Northshire Abbey, this chamber serves as the primary training station for raw human fighters and devout aspirants taking up arms for the Stormwind Army. Here, seasoned battle instructors and paladin mentors teach the basic postures, disciplines, and fundamentals required to defend Elwynn Forest against encroaching kobolds, Defias bandits, and gnoll raiders.

subzone:hall-of-explorers.text: Hall of Explorers. The Hall of Explorers is the sprawling archaeological wing of Ironforge and the bustling headquarters of the dwarven Explorers' League. Part museum, part archive, and part expedition command, it gathers relics, fossils, and ancient tomes from every corner of Azeroth to piece together the forgotten origins of the dwarven race. Occupying the northeastern cavern of Ironforge, the Hall of Explorers—sometimes referred to as the Assembly of Explorers—serves as the nerve center for all Alliance-sanctioned archaeological endeavors. Under the direction of High Explorer Muninn Magellas, scholars and field agents coordinate digs across distant lands, shipping back mysterious relics, ancient titan machinery, and prehistoric bones. The vast Library at its center functions as both a public museum and a restricted storehouse of historical lore.

subzone:heroes-vigil.text: Heroes' Vigil. Heroes' Vigil is a quiet, sacred clearing situated on the central island within Stone Cairn Lake in eastern Elwynn Forest. Centered around a monument known as the Stone of Remembrance, it was dedicated to honor those who fell during the First War. Today, however, the shrine sits largely neglected by Stormwind and is overrun by dangerous renegade wizards. Erected after the First War, Heroes' Vigil centers upon the Stone of Remembrance, an inscribed stone circle meant to honor the soldiers and citizens slaughtered during the Old Horde's sacking of Goldshire and the surrounding valleys. Though once revered as a sacred bastion of faith and sacrifice, the vigil has gradually slipped from the attention of Stormwind's current rulers, leaving its hallowed grounds overgrown and unattended by the realm's soldiers. Because the kingdom has left the island garrisoned by none, outcasts have seized the memorial. A cabal of rogue wizards now controls Stone Cairn Lake and the monument grounds, practicing wild and undisciplined magic away from the oversight of the Kirin Tor and the Academy of Arcane Sciences. The desecration is made all the more bitter by tragic casualties left near the stones, including the body of Henze Faulk, leaving travelers to wonder if the shrine will ever be restored to peace.

subzone:high-seat.text: High Seat. The High Seat is the grand throne room of Ironforge, situated between the Commons and the Great Forge. From this elevated chamber, King Magni Bronzebeard presides over the dwarven realm alongside his royal advisors and historians. The room also houses the sealed passageway leading down into the ancient depths of Old Ironforge. Overlooking the vibrant bustling rings of Ironforge, the High Seat serves as the royal seat of power for the kingdom of Khaz Modan. Within this vaulted chamber, King Magni Bronzebeard hears petitioners, holds council with his advisors, and directs the defense of the Alliance's northern bastions. Flanked by royal dignitaries such as Royal Historian Archesonus and Senator Barin Redstone, the High Seat remains a symbol of unyielding Bronzebeard authority and dwarven resilience amid troubling times across Azeroth. Behind the majestic stone appointments of the throne room lies a heavy doorway leading into the shadowy expanse of Old Ironforge. These lower ruins represent the original, ancestral halls carved out by the dwarves before the city was reconfigured around the Great Forge. Guarded and sealed to general traffic, the portal reminds visitors of the vast antiquity and cavernous history resting beneath the modern capital's stones.

subzone:highperch.text: Highperch. Highperch is an elevated plateau in western Thousand Needles, towering high above the canyon floor. It is renowned as a primary nesting ground for wild wyverns and wind riders. The roost is home to fierce prides defending their young among the windswept crags. Rising sharply out of the canyon floor, Highperch is a rugged sanctuary for Kalimdor's native wyverns. The plateau provides natural defense against predators and an unobstructed launch point for their hunting flights across Thousand Needles. Within its reaches, wyvern prides live under the protection of watchful patriarchs and matriarchs, guarding their nests. The beasts fiercely defend their territory against any intruders who manage to climb into their high domain. While hostile to outsiders, the high cliffs occasionally attract travellers and hunters willing to brave the dangerous ascent. The tauren scout Pao'ka Swiftmountain is stranded on these perilous heights and needs help reaching Whitereach Post. For adventurers journeying through the canyon, scaling the ramp to Highperch means contending with dozens of razor-sharp talons and venomous tails.

subzone:iceflow-lake.text: Iceflow Lake. Iceflow Lake is a frigid, partially frozen body of water situated in western Dun Morogh, directly north of Brewnall Village. Despite the relentless frost, local dwarves maintain fishing holes through the sheet ice to secure fresh water and fish. The snow-covered islands in the center of the lake are prowled by aggressive winter wolves and their alpha, Timber. Spanning western Dun Morogh just outside Brewnall Village, Iceflow Lake battles the bitter Khaz Modan climate year-round. Thick ice sheets continually creep across the surface, forcing local residents like Paxton Ganter to regularly clear holes for ice fishing and drinking water. While the shore provides sustenance, the islands rising from the middle of the lake are far less welcoming. A fierce pack of wild wolves has made these icy mounds their territory, dominated by the notoriously savage gray worg known as Timber.

subzone:iris-lake.text: Iris Lake. Iris Lake is a blighted body of water resting in north-central Ashenvale, east of Astranaar. Once pristine, its waters have turned a sickly yellowish-green from demonic corruption seeping down from Felwood, and hostile bog beasts now prowl its shores. Nestled between Astranaar and the moonwell tended by Shael'dryn, Iris Lake stands as a grim reminder of the wounds inflicted during the Third War. Fel energies drifting south from the tainted heights of Felwood have poisoned the basin, turning its once-clear waters into a foul, sickly yellow-green mire. The corruption has twisted the native plant life and water spirits, raising aggressive bog beasts that lash out at any traveler who wanders near. Despite the severe pollution choking the lake, sacred remnants of the past still linger along its edges. Rare crystalline stones known as Elune's Tears can sometimes be found resting along the muddy banks. Keepers of elven traditions, such as Shael'dryn, seek these holy stones to aid in purifying tainted moonwells and resisting the spreading demonic blight across Ashenvale.

subzone:ironband-s-compound.text: Ironband's Compound. Ironband's Compound is a fortified outpost tucked into the snowy hills south of Helm's Bed Lake in eastern Dun Morogh. Formerly home to the prospector Sturgy Ironband, the camp has been overrun by hostile Dark Iron dwarves who attack anyone venturing too close. Originally established by Sturgy Ironband, this compound south of Helm's Bed Lake once served as a staging post in the snowy wilderness of Dun Morogh. That changed when Dark Iron infiltrators pushed deep into Bronzebeard territory and seized the site for themselves. Now bristling with hostile dwarves, the compound serves as an enemy forward base threatening travelers and nearby settlements, right under the nose of Ironforge. The presence of a fortified Dark Iron camp within Dun Morogh's own borders is a serious provocation. Ironforge keeps a wary eye on the compound, dispatching seasoned warriors to recover fallen scouts and secure vital intelligence proving the extent of the Dark Iron threat in the mountain kingdom.

subzone:ironband-s-excavation-site.text: Ironband's Excavation Site. Ironband's Excavation Site is an expansive dwarven dig located in southeastern Loch Modan, just south of the lake and southwest of Farstrider Lodge. Led by Prospector Ironband, the archaeological operation was abruptly halted when aggressive, volatile troggs overran the trenches. Spurred by the dwarven drive to uncover their ancient Titan origins, Prospector Ironband established this sprawling digsite along the rugged cliffs of southeastern Loch Modan. What began as a promising excavation quickly turned into a disaster when the digging disturbed an unusually fierce and large breed of subterranean troggs. The creatures surged from the earth, driving back the miners and setting up camp amidst the scattered tools, broken carts, and half-excavated relics. Much like archaeological efforts in the Badlands, Wetlands, and Uldaman, the site sits in dangerous limbo. Surviving prospectors cling to the edges of the perimeter, desperate to reclaim their stolen gear and protect exposed artifacts—including strange ancient statues left behind by long-forgotten builders—from being smashed or carried off by the ravenous trogg infestation.

subzone:ironforge-airfield.text: Ironforge Airfield. Tucked away high in the snowy peaks northeast of Ironforge, this remote dwarven airstrip serves as a proving ground and staging area for gnome flying machines and dwarven mountaineers. Unmarked by main roads, the plateau overlooks the jagged crags of Dun Morogh and the steep descent toward the Wetlands. Perched far above the beaten trails of Dun Morogh, the high-altitude airfield is a quiet marvel of Alliance cooperation. Sheltered by surrounding mountain peaks, dwarven masonry anchors the blustery ridgelines while gnomish flying machines sit parked along open landing strips. Mountaineers keep watch over the perimeter alongside engineers busy wrenching gears and inspecting steam-belching engines in the biting cold. Despite its isolation, the airfield is far from serene. The surrounding valley features frozen waters and crags contested by Frostmane trolls, who dwell in nearby caves and constantly harass the dwarven sentries. In the shadow of the peaks, dwarven defenders and Stormpike patrols clash regularly with troll raiders across the ice, keeping the remote installation in a state of quiet, vigilant standoff.

subzone:jansen-stead.text: Jansen Stead. Jansen Stead is the northernmost farmstead in Westfall, situated just down the road from the bridge to Elwynn Forest. Like much of the surrounding breadbasket, the homestead has fallen out of peasant hands and is swarming with rogue mechanical Harvest Watchers and roving Defias bandits. Positioned right past the Elwynn border, the Jansen Stead represents the harsh reality greeting anyone traveling westward into Westfall. Once a flourishing family farm feeding the kingdom, its rightful occupants have been driven away by the rising tide of unrest. In their place, hostile Harvest Watchers—mechanical constructs associated with the Defias Brotherhood—patrol the blighted fields alongside brigands. Its proximity to the main road makes it a prominent early hazard for couriers and travelers moving between Goldshire and Sentinel Hill.

subzone:jasperlode-mine.text: Jasperlode Mine. Jasperlode Mine is an iron and mineral excavation in north-central Elwynn Forest that once supplied Stormwind City with vital resources. Today, the shafts are overrun by swarming kobolds and deadly giant spiders, leaving the resource-strapped kingdom unable to reclaim it. Jasperlode Mine was historically one of Stormwind's most productive mining operations, providing steady mineral wealth alongside nearby Fargodeep. With the kingdom's military stretched thin defending against external threats and unrest, local garrisons have been unable to protect the shafts. Kobolds seized the opportunity to burrow inside, driving human miners out and stockpiling stolen gold and tallow candles. The infestation within Jasperlode extends beyond simple vermin. In the deepest, darkest corridors beneath the timber supports, an aggressive colony of mine spiders has taken root. Led by a massive matriarch known to locals as Mother Fang, the spiders treat trespassing kobolds—and any unwary prospectors—as effortless prey, making any attempt to salvage the mine exceptionally hazardous.

subzone:kargathia-keep.text: Kargathia Keep. Kargathia Keep is a fortified Horde stronghold anchoring the eastern front of the Warsong Lumber Camp in Ashenvale. Serving as headquarters for the outpost's overseers, it guards the river border and ensures rapid reinforcement lines directly back to Orgrimmar. Perched on the eastern edge of the Warsong Lumber Camp just west of the Southfury River, Kargathia Keep serves as the command center for the Horde's logging operations in Ashenvale. Upgraded with heavy spiked barricades, this fortified outpost houses Overseer Gorthak and his officers. Its strategic position against the river border allows the Warsong clan to monitor incoming incursions and receive swift reinforcements directly from the neighboring lands of Durotar and Orgrimmar whenever night elf skirmishers strike. Like the fortress of Kargath in the Badlands and Bladefist Bay along the coast of Durotar, the outpost takes its name from the famed chieftain Kargath Bladefist. For the Warsong orcs braving Ashenvale's hostile woodlands, the keep's imposing classic architecture stands as an enduring symbol of martial resilience and Horde defiance in territory claimed by the night elves.

subzone:kharanos.text: Kharanos. Kharanos is a bustling mountain settlement nestled in the snowy heart of Dun Morogh, just down the road from Ironforge. Serving as the primary hub for travelers leaving Coldridge Valley, the town hosts a forge, gnomish workshops, and the famous Thunderbrew Distillery. Situated along the central road of Dun Morogh, Kharanos is the first true town welcoming recruits arriving from Anvilmar. Despite the biting cold and biting winds, the settlement thrives thanks to local dwarven grit and gnomish ingenuity. It centers around a roaring public forge and the Thunderbrew Distillery, renowned across the eastern mountains for producing some of the finest ale in Khaz Modan. Between bustling crafters and weary travelers seeking warmth, the town stands as the essential staging ground for business in the lower peaks. Behind its cozy hearths, Kharanos serves as a vital military outpost tasked with keeping the mountain passes secure. Fierce indigenous wendigo prowl the frozen caverns directly to the west, while aggressive Frostmane trolls remain entrenched atop Shimmer Ridge to the northwest. With Ironforge's regular forces stretched thin across the realm, the town relies heavily on visiting adventurers and local watchmen to drive back raiding parties, cull dangerous predators, and ensure the trade routes remain open.

subzone:lake-falathim.text: Lake Falathim. Lake Falathim is a tranquil body of water nestled in the forested hills of western Ashenvale, southwest of Maestra's Post. Revered for the constant touch of Elune's moonlight upon its surface day and night, it was once a beloved retreat for night elves. In recent days, however, aggressive murlocs have overrun its shores, turning a sacred haven into a perilous hazard. Tucked away southeast of the Zoram Strand, Lake Falathim was long cherished by the Kaldorei as a peaceful sanctuary for swimming and fishing. According to local lore, the gentle radiance of Elune rests upon these waters at all hours, day or night. Despite this sacred blessing, ferocious murlocs have surged inland to seize the shores, nesting in thick numbers and driving away local travelers and scholars alike. The sudden occupation by murlocs has made the lake deadly to solitary wanderers. The night elf scholar Teronis was recently lost somewhere near the water's edge on a mission of inquiry. Given the savage hostility of the amphibians lurking on the banks and in the shallows, the Sentinels fear the worst for any who venture toward the moonlit pool alone.

subzone:lakeridge-highway.text: Lakeridge Highway. Lakeridge Highway is an old thoroughfare running along the southern shore of Lake Everstill in the Redridge Mountains. Once a vital and heavily traveled artery prior to the First War, it has fallen into ruin and disuse. Today, roving packs of gnolls and Blackrock orcs make passage along the road perilous for travelers. Before the devastation of the First War, the Lakeridge Highway served as a bustling trade corridor through Redridge, carrying goods and folk along the southern banks of Lake Everstill. In those peaceful days, travelers could journey between the valley settlements and the eastern heights under the protection of the Kingdom of Stormwind. That safety shattered when the Horde marched through the region, leaving eastern Redridge contested and desolate. Following the seizure of Stonewatch Keep by Blackrock orcs, regular maintenance and patrols along the highway ceased entirely. The road quickly deteriorated into an overgrown track contested by savage gnoll packs. With Stormwind's military spread thin and unable to reinforce Lakeshire, the highway remains officially unsafe. Any traveler seeking to reach the eastern ridges must now carve a path through gnoll ambushes.

subzone:lakeshire-inn.text: Lakeshire Inn. The Lakeshire Inn is the social hub and primary refuge in the beleaguered town of Lakeshire. Situated in the heart of the Redridge Mountains, it provides warmth, ale, and safe lodging for local townsfolk and weary travelers contending with the surrounding perils. Perched on the shore of Lake Everstill, the Lakeshire Inn offers a brief respite from the gnoll bands and Blackrock orcs pressing in on the town. Despite Lakeshire's increasingly desperate military situation, the tavern maintains a cozy, bustling atmosphere. Barkeep Daniels and Innkeeper Brianna attend to the locals and travelers, serving up flagons of ale, wine, and warm meals. It is a vital meeting point where townspeople trade news, drown their sorrows, and seek hired blades to help defend the eastern border of the kingdom. Beyond ordinary patrons nursing drinks at the counter, the inn draws a variety of colorful figures. Wiley the Black watches the room from a table, keeping his own counsel and keeping tabs on regional dangers. Traveling brewers like Yorus Barleybrew make stops here, while Darcy Parker and other townsfolk frequent the common room. For adventurers venturing further into the jagged peaks or heading south toward Duskwood, the inn is the final bastion of civilization and safety before entering contested wilderness.

subzone:lakeshire-town-hall.text: Lakeshire Town Hall. Lakeshire Town Hall serves as the administrative seat of the Redridge Mountains, standing at the heart of the lakeside settlement. Inside, Magistrate Solomon oversees local governance while wrestling with relentless threats from Blackrock orcs and gnolls. Lakeshire Town Hall is an aging stone structure that has been diligently refurbished multiple times over the years. Positioned prominently within Lakeshire, it houses Magistrate Solomon, a kind and dedicated civil leader tasked with maintaining order in the eastern reaches of the Kingdom of Stormwind. With Stormwind's military resources stretched thin and royal aid scarce, the hall has transformed from a quiet administrative office into an active command center where desperate appeals for volunteer defenders and mercenaries are processed daily. Gnoll incursions and the encroaching Blackrock orcs have pushed Solomon to desperation. With aid scarce, the magistrate readily accepts help from independent adventurers who come through the town hall doors.

subzone:library-ironforge.text: Library (Ironforge). Tucked inside the eastern wing of the Hall of Explorers, the Library serves as Ironforge's foremost repository of historical knowledge, archeological relics, and ancient lore. Maintained diligently by the Explorers' League, it houses extensive historical tomes alongside rare artifacts recovered from digs across Azeroth. Occupying a massive chamber within the Hall of Explorers, the Library is where dwarven scholars sift through the relics and field reports recovered by adventurers across the world. Administered by the Explorers' League, the shelves are packed with foundational chronicles detailing the War of the Three Hammers, the ancient Troll Wars, and the origins of the dwarven race. Inquiries regarding rare books or archival locations are directed to Librarian Mae Paledust. Beyond rows of dense bookshelves, the Library doubles as a working museum overseen by Curator Thorius. Here, physical specimens collected from deep excavations, abandoned ruins, and distant shorelines are analyzed, preserved, and displayed. The League's curators preserve everything from crude murloc idols and carved knives to mysterious relics recovered frozen in northern ice, cataloging each find to piece together the hidden history of the Titans and early Azeroth.

subzone:long-wash.text: Long Wash. The Long Wash is a bleak, windswept stretch of beach in Darkshore running just south of Auberdine toward the ruins of Ameth'Aran. Gloomy and scattered with marine carcasses and flotsam, the shoreline has recently grown dangerous due to an increasing presence of hostile murlocs. Despite its name, the Long Wash is actually the shortest distinct stretch of coastline in Darkshore. It sits under the region's perpetual overcast skies, an expanse of damp sand littered with flotsam, beached driftwood, and the carcasses of sea creatures washed up by the Veiled Sea. While local crabs comb through the surf, travelers southward from Auberdine must tread cautiously: murloc tribes have established camps along the water's edge, aggressively attacking anyone encroaching on their scavenged territory.

subzone:maestra-s-post.text: Maestra's Post. Maestra's Post is a small Alliance settlement in western Ashenvale, perched along the road northwest of Astranaar and south of the Ruins of Ordil'Aran. Guarded by night elven Sentinels and hosting a rare human presence in Kalimdor's ancient forest, it serves as a forward watch against encroaching threats. Positioned under the canopy of western Ashenvale, Maestra's Post consists of a slender night elven tower and an open lodge. It sits as an essential waypoint for travelers marching between the coast of Darkshore and the larger hub of Astranaar. Despite its tranquil elven architecture, the outpost stands perpetually on edge. The local Sentinels keep a wary eye on the surrounding wilderness, where corrupted furbolg stir and nearby Horde movements constantly threaten the Alliance's supply lines. Unlike many insular night elf enclaves deep within the woods, Maestra's Post is notable for housing a handful of human allies. Figures such as Feero Ironhand and Delgren the Purifier dwell alongside the Sentinels here, lending their martial strength and devotion to the holy Light in service to the broader Alliance. Their presence makes this remote campsite one of the earliest meeting grounds between the eastern kingdoms and the ancient defenders of Kalimdor.

subzone:malaka-jin.text: Malaka'jin. Malaka'jin is a small Horde encampment nestled in the lower hills of the Stonetalon Mountains, just south of the Grimtotem Post. Inhabited primarily by Darkspear troll hunters, the settlement serves as a rustic waystation and hunting outpost for travelers ascending into the rugged peaks from the Barrens. Tucked away near the main path into the Stonetalon Mountains, Malaka'jin provides a welcome sanctuary for Horde wanderers venturing into contested heights. The village is home to a band of rugged troll hunters who eke out a living off the crags and scrublands. While living modestly, these hunters offer supplies, trade their fresh game to weary adventurers, and keep a wary eye on the hostile mountain wildlife and the belligerent Grimtotem tauren lurking further up the trails. Perched precariously near the boundary of the Barrens, Malaka'jin marks one of the earliest Horde presences established in Stonetalon. Though small and quiet compared to the major fortress at Sun Rock Retreat further north, it functions as a vital logistical anchor, allowing Horde trackers to monitor tribal unrest and secure the winding roads against encroaching threats.

subzone:master-s-glaive.text: Master's Glaive. The Master's Glaive is an ancient, unsettling landmark tucked into southwestern Darkshore where a colossal adamantine weapon stands impaled in a massive petrified skull. Long revered by local night elves as a sacred mystery, the site now swarms with Twilight's Hammer cultists drawn to the lingering malevolence of an ancient entity. Rising out of the Darkshore earth, the Master's Glaive is a massive adamantine blade buried deep in a colossal petrified skull. No record names the creature that died here or the hand that drove the blade home. Onu, the Ancient of Lore, says only that an old, old lord of the earth fell on this spot, and the night elves long believed that only the titans could have wielded so gigantic a weapon. Today, the impaled monolith stands as a stark, petrified monument to that forgotten struggle. Though the site was held in solemn reverence by night elves for generations, sinister forces have recently seized the grounds. Fanatics of the Twilight's Hammer cult have established a camp around the sunken carcass, carving out trenches and uncovering petrified ribs. Drawn by whispers beneath the stone, the cultists obsessively study the remains and commune with the malevolent power that still clings to the ancient remains, seeking to revive or harness whatever fell essence slumbers within the earth.

subzone:military-ward.text: Military Ward. The Military Ward serves as the martial heart of Ironforge, housing the city's command infrastructure, weapons masters, and barracks. Marked by bold red banners, it is where dwarven soldiers, hunters, and siege engineers train alongside mechanized siege engines and flying machines. Situated within the northern perimeter of the mountain fortress, the Military Ward concentrates Ironforge's defensive forces into a bustling staging ground. The central complex, the Hall of Arms, accommodates warrior and hunter trainers, battlemasters, and hangars housing dwarven flying machines and steam tanks. Surrounding the drill squares and training dummies are supply outlets such as Craghelm's Plate and Chain, Goldfury's Hunting Supplies, and Timberline Arms, making the ward the primary staging point for mountaineers and city defenders. Distinguished from the pale blue of the Commons and the fiery orange of the Great Forge, the Military Ward is draped in martial red banners. Between drills and weapons inspections, soldiers and off-duty guards gather at Bruuk's Corner for an ale, while Weapon Master Buliwyf Stonehand instructs recruits in ancient dwarven martial traditions.

subzone:mirage-raceway.text: Mirage Raceway. The Mirage Raceway is an impromptu engineering proving ground situated in the shimmering salt flats of Thousand Needles. Founded on the heated rivalry between goblin tinkerer Pozzik and gnome engineer Fizzle Brassbolts, it pits high-speed rocket cars against one another across the baked earth. The track serves as a neutral gathering place where members of both the Alliance and Horde come to wager, tinker, and cheer on their favored machines. Sprawled across the vast white desert floor of the Shimmering Flats, the Mirage Raceway was born out of an unrelenting grudge match between two master tinkerers: the goblin Pozzik and the gnome Fizzle Brassbolts. Determined to settle once and for all whose race possesses superior technical ingenuity, the two constructed custom rocket-powered drag cars and recruited rival crews to pit them against each other in daily high-velocity showdowns. The relentless competition has turned the barren flats into a bustling hub of invention, sabotage, and testing as each crew desperately looks for any mechanical advantage. The raceway draws supporters from both the Horde and Alliance. Spectators gather from across Kalimdor to cheer on either gnome precision or goblin firepower, while gamblers and shady opportunists thrive on the constant wagers placed on the results. Beyond the roar of rocket thrusters, the camps serve as a busy trading depot for travelers journeying between Thousand Needles and the blazing sands of Tanaris.

subzone:mirkfallon-lake.text: Mirkfallon Lake. Mirkfallon Lake sits in a central highland basin in the Stonetalon Mountains, nestled beneath the sheer cliffs of Windshear Crag. Its waters and surrounding banks teem with native wildlife, including aggressive slimes, roaming thunder lizards, and descending wyverns. Positioned at the geographic center of the Stonetalon range, Mirkfallon Lake rests between the mountain passes leading south toward the Webwinder Path and north toward Stonetalon Peak. Fed by highland runoff, the lake offers a fertile oasis amidst the craggy peaks, drawing thunder lizards down to drink and wyverns from their roosts high above. The waters are also inhabited by strange, bubbling slimes, turning an otherwise serene mountain tarn into a hazardous crossing for lone travelers. Paths crisscross the lake basin in all directions. To the east, rocky tracks ascend into Windshear Crag and the logging operations running deep into the forested valleys. Travelers pressing north past the lake climb toward night elven sanctums and tauren heights, while those skirting south must contend with venomous spider hollows. As a result, the shores of Mirkfallon Lake often serve as an unpredictable crossing point for explorers and scouts navigating the contested mountains.

subzone:mist-s-edge.text: Mist's Edge. Mist's Edge is the long, windswept coastline stretching north from Auberdine along western Darkshore. Shrouded in damp ocean fog, these gray beaches are littered with shipwrecks, colossal sea creature remains, and roving packs of crabs and murlocs. Running along the western edge of Darkshore, Mist's Edge is defined by damp sands, rocky tidepools, and perpetual coastal fog. The beach is a graveyard of the sea, littered with decaying sea behemoths, drift timber, and the shattered ribs of wrecked vessels. While seemingly barren, the coastline teems with shoreline scavengers, notably aggressive crabs and territorial murloc tribes that nest in the surf. The treacherous waters off the coast of Darkshore have claimed countless vessels, depositing shattered hulls and discarded cargo all along the sands. Night elf sentinels and local scavengers keep a wary eye on the coastline, where opportunistic murloc encampments frequently menace travelers heading up and down the coast from Auberdine.

subzone:mo-grosh-stronghold.text: Mo'grosh Stronghold. Mo'grosh Stronghold is a fortified den of ogres dug into the northeastern hills of Loch Modan. Nestled among ancient, weathered ruins, these brutal giants pose a constant threat to the dwarven settlements below. Tucked away in the crags of northeastern Loch Modan, Mo'grosh Stronghold serves as the primary base for the Mo'grosh clan of ogres in the region. The brute forces lurking within the caves and outer camps raid traveling dwarven supply caravans and present an enduring danger to the peace of Thelsamar. The rugged stonework scattered around the camp suggests the site once belonged to an older settlement, before the lumbering ogres claimed the territory and raised their distinctive mounds.

subzone:moonbrook-schoolhouse.text: Moonbrook Schoolhouse. Standing in the northwestern corner of Moonbrook, the Schoolhouse is a prominent building resembling a town hall with a small graveyard behind it. Originally erected to educate local children under headmaster Stalvan Mistmantle, it now stands derelict amidst the Defias occupation of Westfall. Before Moonbrook fell to ruin and bandits, the community invested in the education of its youth by raising this grand schoolhouse. After Stalvan Mistmantle began tutoring local children, the mayor commissioned him to run a school. In those brighter days, the hall bustled with students rather than thieves, standing as proof of Moonbrook's former prosperity. Now, the schoolhouse lies abandoned to the elements and infested with outlaws, while the weathered headstones of its rear cemetery silently oversee Westfall's steady decay.

subzone:moonspray.text: Moonspray. The Moonspray is an Alliance transport vessel belonging to the Kaldorei Fleet. It provides essential maritime passage across the waters separating mainland Kalimdor from the great World Tree, Teldrassil. The Moonspray serves as an indispensable lifeline between the docks of Auberdine on Darkshore's coast and Rut'theran Village at the root of Teldrassil. Traversing the Veiled Sea, the transport carries adventurers, couriers, and vital provisions between the isolated night elf sanctuary in the crown of the World Tree and the ancient mainland of Kalimdor.

subzone:mor-shan-rampart.text: Mor'shan Rampart. The Mor'shan Rampart is a heavily fortified Horde barricade positioned at the northern border of the Barrens, guarding the entrance to Ashenvale. Constructed primarily by the Warsong clan, it shields Horde territory from night elf counterattacks while serving as a staging ground for incursions deeper into the forest. Standing at the northern terminus of the Gold Road, the Mor'shan Rampart marks the transition between the arid plains of the Barrens and the ancient canopies of Ashenvale. Built from heavy timber, defensive palisades, and fortified watchtowers, this bulwark was raised to stem the retaliatory strikes of night elven forces outraged by the Horde's logging operations. It acts both as a shield securing the northern gate to Kalimdor's interior and as a forward staging post for raiding parties pushing north toward Astranaar. Manned primarily by battle-hardened fighters affiliated with the Warsong clan, the rampart remains under constant military readiness. From these parapets, sentries monitor the tree line for night elf scouts and archers, keeping open supply lines between the frontline outposts of Ashenvale and the greater Horde settlements to the south.

subzone:mortwake-s-tower.text: Klaven's Tower. Klaven's Tower, also called the Defias Tower, is a fortified watchtower standing near the river in southeastern Westfall. Commanded by the rogue Klaven Mortwake, it serves as a critical waypoint for smuggling stolen goods across kingdom borders. Perched on the borderlands north of the Dagger Hills, Klaven's Tower is a vital hub for Defias Brotherhood operations in southern Westfall. Together with Jerod's Landing across the river in Elwynn Forest, the site acts as a receiving post and staging ground for contraband plundered from the Redridge Mountains. Its commanding vantage over the waterways allows the Brotherhood to slip supplies past Kingdom patrols, shielding their logistical network from the crown's eyes.

subzone:nightsong-woods.text: Nightsong Woods. Nightsong Woods forms the embattled eastern expanse of Ashenvale, reaching from Raynewood Retreat toward the borders of Azshara. It serves as the primary battleground between the night elves defending their sacred forest and the Warsong clan harvesting lumber for the Horde. Across its shadowed glades, ancient groves clash with fortified encampments amidst persistent demonic corruption. Stretching eastward across Ashenvale to Azshara, Nightsong Woods is defined by escalating violence. The Falfarren River bisects the western reaches, creating a volatile boundary between Alliance settlements and Horde encroachments. Further east, the forest fractures into heavily disputed territories where Splintertree Post coordinates Horde campaigns against the Silverwing Sentinels. Orcish axes continuously clear southern groves to fuel the Horde's expansion, leaving clear-cut swaths that infuriate the Kaldorei. Adding to the peril, satyr strongholds like Satyrnaar and Xavian, alongside demonic remnants in Demon Fall Canyon and Felfire Hill, taint the eastern canopies.

subzone:northshire-valley.text: Northshire Valley. Tucked away in the northern mountains of Elwynn Forest, Northshire Valley serves as the peaceful cradle and training ground for the kingdom of Stormwind's newest defenders. Surrounded by natural barriers, it hosts the historic Northshire Abbey, fertile vineyards, and the rich Echo Ridge Mine. Despite its tranquil appearance, the valley faces mounting unrest from rogue bandits, infesting kobolds, and displaced predators. Northshire Valley is framed by nearly impassable mountain ridges, with its only road heading south through a fortified gatehouse toward Goldshire and the rest of Elwynn Forest. A clear river winds through its pastures before feeding south into Crystal Lake. At the valley's heart stands Northshire Abbey, an ancient sanctuary where the Holy Light is taught and where recruits are trained by the Knights of the Silver Hand and seasoned veterans. Beyond the abbey walls lie the bountiful Northshire Vineyards and Echo Ridge Mine, forming a self-sustaining pocket of Stormwind territory that feels far removed from the wider world's wars. Even this sheltered haven has felt the strain of Stormwind's overextended defenses. Marshal McBride and his detachment of the Stormwind Guard struggle to maintain order across the vale. Packs of wolves driven north from blighted Duskwood prowl the surrounding woods, while vermin-like kobolds have overrun the tunnels of Echo Ridge Mine. Worse still, masked thugs aligned with the Defias Brotherhood openly harass the vineyards and threaten the abbey's grounds, forcing local commanders to recruit every able-bodied civilian arriving at their gates.

subzone:old-town.text: Old Town. Old Town is the oldest and grittiest quarter of Stormwind City, having largely survived the destruction of the First War intact. Rather than gleaming stone plazas, its narrow alleys feature weathered brick, working-class tenements, and bustling military facilities. It serves as home to the kingdom's military Command Center as well as the clandestine headquarters of SI:7. While the rest of Stormwind was painstakingly rebuilt from the ground up by the Stonemasons following the First War, Old Town escaped total ruin. Because it did not require wholesale reconstruction, it never received the pristine marble facades and grand canals seen in the Trade District or Cathedral Square. Instead, it remains a rustic, crowded quarter where working folk, laborers, and the city's poorest residents reside. Its cobbled streets are narrower, dirtier, and far more chaotic than the rest of the capital, yet they preserve the authentic atmosphere of pre-war Stormwind. Behind its weathered tenements, Old Town functions as the martial backbone of the Alliance capital. The Command Center houses Stormwind's military officers, barracks, and combat trainers, alongside the Champions' Hall where the Alliance's finest warriors gather. Tucked away toward the district's edge sits the covert compound of SI:7, the kingdom's secretive intelligence agency led by Master Mathias Shaw. Off-duty footmen and shadowy operatives alike gather at the Pig and Whistle Tavern, rubbing shoulders in one of the city's liveliest watering holes.

subzone:oracle-glade.text: Oracle Glade. Nestled in northwestern Teldrassil, the Oracle Glade is a sacred woodland sanctuary home to the wondrous Oracle Tree and the World Tree's premier moonwell. Despite its serene purpose as a center of communion and vigilance, the glade faces constant harassment from encroaching Bloodfeather harpies. The Oracle Glade rests quietly between Darnassus and Wellspring Lake, serving as a vital nexus of night elven communion with nature. At its center stands the Oracle Tree, an ancient specimen whose massive boughs evoke the silhouette of an eagle perched atop a bear. Nearby shimmers the first and most potent of Teldrassil's sacred moonwells, an oasis of lunar magic bathed in Elune's grace. Alongside the Circle of the Ancients, the Oracle Tree watches over the island boughs, shedding inscribed bark that acts as vital communiques to Archdruid Fandral Staghelm regarding the World Tree's health. The glade's tranquility is fragile. Aggressive Bloodfeather harpies have descended upon the grove, establishing roosts among the high branches and threatening the sacred tree. Sentinels dispatched from Darnassus struggle to root out the avian scavengers, who actively harass traveling druids and taint the natural serenity of the moonwell. Travelers passing through the northern boughs must tread lightly, as the harpies strike swiftly at any who venture near their roosts.

subzone:park.text: Park. Tucked along the western edge of Stormwind City between Cathedral Square and the Mage Quarter, the Park is a lush sanctuary of greenery and quiet reflection. Devoted to nature and leisure amidst the bustling stone capital, it serves as the primary haven for visiting night elves and houses the only druid trainers in the Eastern Kingdoms. While the rest of Stormwind is dominated by cobbled walkways, towering limestone ramparts, and crowded market stalls, the Park offers a tranquil breath of wilderness.
